output: On April 23, a Russian SU-27 fighter flew in a provocative manner close to a US RC-135U plane conducting a routine mission over the Sea of Okhotsk, by approaching and crossing the nose of the US aircraft, followed by manifesting that it was armed with air-to-air missiles. This occurred amid escalating tensions between the US and Russia over Russia's involvement in Ukraine, where President Obama had earlier denounced Russian "aggression".

The Prince of Wales, Charles, and his wife Camilla are embarking on a 12-day tour to celebrate Charles' 67th birthday, visiting 12 different towns and cities across Australia and New Zealand, marking his 15th visit to Australia, with a possible meeting with the Australian Prime Minister.
A 70-year-old woman was attacked in Sneem, County Kerry, on September 20, while a man was detained and questioned at the Killarney Garda (police) station following an incident on a subsequent day.
Hugh McGoldrick, a former GP, had his name removed from the medical register after admitting falsifying drug trials on sleep disorder patients, as no appeal was submitted within the 28-day deadline.
A 21-year-old man is being held on suspicion of murder, after a body was found in a wooded area in Dorking, Surrey Police are awaiting a post-mortem examination for identification and cause of death.

A 25-year-old man named Josh Hanson was fatally stabbed at the RE bar in Eastcote, Hillingdon, and died at the scene shortly after 01:10 BST on Sunday. Scotland Yard is urging anyone who was in the bar or the Field End Road area at around 01:00 Sunday to contact them with any potential information, as no arrests have been made yet.

The article discusses a proposed new service between Sandown and Southsea, aimed at boosting tourism to the Isle of Wight, with the possibility of the service operating two days a week in July and August, subject to permits and discussions with local authorities.

A 30-year-old man was arrested following an attack by up to eight individuals on a victim in the Heights area at approximately 02:00 BST on Sunday, and the police have urged for any related information about the incident.

In India, floods have caused the death of over 200 people in Assam, affected 450,000 people, and displaced many more. The Prime Minister has announced aid packages and plans to visit Assam in search of a long-term solution to the annual flooding. Meanwhile, some affected people in Gujarat have started to return to their villages.

The 25th anniversary season of the Premier League starts with Arsenal hosting Leicester City on Friday 11 August, with Sky Sports holding the rights to broadcast 10 Friday night matches, while a significant portion of football fans reported using unofficial online streams for matches.

Footballer Cristian Montano, aged 22, was dismissed by Oldham Athletic after a thorough investigation into spot-fixing, with the club acting swiftly and seriously, despite it being a difficult week for them.

A 20-year-old man was given a suspended jail sentence and supervision order for accidentally starting and causing extensive damage to a 42-acre former Pontins resort in Brixham, including the demolition of the arcade area, pool area, and ballroom, and increasing the demolition cost due to the presence of asbestos due to the fire's rapid spread.

Scottish athlete Robert Wilson, 30, returned to Nottingham Forest from Celtic for £2.5m in 2013 for a second stint that spanned 51 appearances, but has since been without a team following his release in 2021. Prior to his time at Forest, Wilson had playing experience at Preston North End and Notts County.

Australia left-arm seamer Faulkner took 3 wickets (3-45) including key dismissals of Kusal Perera, Angelo Mathews, and Thisara Perera, while debutant Sri Lankan slow left-armer Amila Aponso shone with 4-18 as Sri Lanka made 288 in Colombo. After Matthew Wade scored 76, Australia was bowled out for 206 in reply, resulting in a 82-run win for Sri Lanka, leveling the five-match bilateral series at 1-1.

The 32-year-old rugby player Vadim Cobilas, the first Moldova international to play in the Premiership, is leaving Sale and moving to France's Top 14, with his position set to be filled by advanced talks with David Seymour, Will Addison, and Mark Jennings for new deals at the club. Tommy Taylor is not yet decided about his future, while Wasps is reportedly interested in him, and recruitment for next season is already underway at Sale.

India, cruising towards their highest successful run-chase in Australia with consecutive centuries from Shikhar Dhawan and Virat Kohli, suffered a dramatic collapse from 277-1 to 323 all out due to Kane Richardson's 5-68, with India now facing a 4-1 series defeat and Australia aiming for a whitewash in the final match in Sydney.

The Hammersmith and City Line and partially the Circle Line have been temporarily suspended due to the London Fire Brigade's request, fearing potential debris could fall onto the tracks, caused by a fire at a 24-story block in London, with 58 deaths currently presumed, and teams are working to secure the debris for the lines to reopen.
Scottish footballer Jamie Hamill, previously a right-back and midfielder for Kilmarnock and Hearts, returns to Rugby Park after three years, signing a contract extending his tenure until 2017.
Ross Morgan, an excited Ipswich fan, accidentally punched a hole in the ceiling while celebrating Paul Anderson's goal against Norwich, with Anderson later offering to cover the repair costs.

Retailers in Wales are now compelled to hide tobacco products from public view, with fines and imprisonment possible for violations, in an effort to reduce visual access and lessen appeal, thereby potentially improving public health.

The 20-year-old footballer named Lucas, who has previously played for the National League side and scored three goals in 10 appearances, is brought into the Bristol Rovers squad in League Two, with manager Luke Garrard suggesting he will provide options in the forward areas due to his ability to score goals and disrupt defenses.

Knaresborough station in North Yorkshire is undergoing renovation, including waterproofing and the removal and rebuilding of the chimney stack on the signal box, with the platform work scheduled at night to reduce inconvenience, as the station is a historically significant site.

Former NFL player Lawrence Phillips, known for his troubles both on and off the field, is believed to have committed suicide early on Wednesday, after being implicated in the death of his former cellmate and facing trial by a judge over the case.

The article discusses the extension of bus lane hours for Belfast Rapid Transit (BRT), starting at 7:00 and ending at 19:00, and a subsequent two-round consultation on the proposal to ensure maximum compliance and minimize confusion, with potential adjustments like loading and unloading windows based on stakeholder and community input.

In a crucial La Liga match, Messi bypassed the first two games without scoring for Barcelona, entering as a substitute after a family matter on Friday. Despite a slow start and a deficit to Atletico Madrid, he equalized with a free-kick and claimed the winner, hitting 287 career La Liga goals for Barca, surpassing the competition record. Cristiano Ronaldo also scored five goals on the same day to break the Madrid record.

Over 70 individuals, including football players and directors from 30 clubs in lower Italian leagues, have been detained amid allegations of match-fixing, with possible links to the 'Ndrangheta crime syndicate, and a police officer is among those under suspicion in the ongoing investigation.

Spiderlings, hybrid species from Sussex and Suffolk, were released in Castle Marshes to increase genetic variability and adaptability in the new population, with the aim of helping them better survive the impacts of climate change, supported by organizations like Natural England, Suffolk Wildlife Trust, and the BBC Wildlife Fund.

The Partition of India in 1947 led to the formation of two new independent countries (Pakistan and Bangladesh), and the event resulted in widespread displacement, with millions of people becoming refugees, including the family detailed in a Newsround special on CBBC.

Iva Barr, a seasoned marathon runner who participated in the first London Marathon in 1981, attempted her 20th marathon, completing approximately 14 miles before deciding to finish the rest of the course on foot and by public transport, expressing satisfaction with her experience despite not completing the full distance.

In China's top cities, the extreme competition in the property market has prompted some couples to resort to fake divorces to purchase additional homes, despite efforts by the central bank to curb rising prices and address concerns of young workers with lower wages.

A 24-year-old individual is under arrest in connection with the death of landlord Mr Jones, 46, who passed away at The Blossoms public house in Holyhead. The police are conducting investigations, have made an appeal to witnesses who were on an Arriva bus on a specific route on Friday, and are not releasing the cause of death yet. A family tribute was given for Mr Jones describing him as a loved partner, soul mate, father, brother, uncle, and friend.
The article invites readers to connect with BBC News Entertainment through various social media platforms, and encourages them to submit their story suggestions to a specific email address.

A fatal two-vehicle collision occurred in Drumjohn, near Carsphairn, involving a red Ford Fiesta and a white Asda delivery van, claiming the lives of drivers Antony Sztuka, 50, and Scott Kennedy, 46, both from Ayrshire. Police are eager to speak with a potential witness who was on the A713 at the time and may have information useful to the investigation.

Australian rowing athlete Sarah Tait, who won a silver medal in the 2012 London Olympics, was an inspiration to her fellow athletes and in the sports community, despite being diagnosed with cervical cancer in 2013, and is remembered for her extraordinary achievements, including her Olympic medal, and her warm personality.

A suicide bomber, believed to be affiliated with the Taliban, attacked a second army bus in Kabul by the new Afghan President Ashraf Ghani, injuring four soldiers and civilians. This attack occurred a day after Ghani approved a deal with US officials allowing US troops to stay in Afghanistan, following previous disputes between the US and his predecessor, Hamid Karzai.

Daimler, the parent company of Mercedes-Benz, forecasts significant growth in its full-year sales despite a slower rise in sales of Mercedes cars in China, with expectations of modest growth in key emerging markets like China and India. Despite the cooling market in China, Daimler's CEO, Dieter Zetsche, remains optimistic about the company's prospects and its capacity to continue growing, based on strong performance in the second quarter.
A 10-year-old Danish prince was rescued from a dangerous rip current at Mermaid Beach by lifeguard Nick Malcolm, who could have prevented a potential fatal outcome according to his supervisor.

Emergency services responded to a nonsuspicious house fire where an elderly man's body was discovered at the intersection of Elgin Road and Inchbroom Road on Wednesday at 16:10, with no reported injuries to others and the man's identity yet to be disclosed.

Veterans with complex amputation-related medical issues are now receiving treatment at the Defence Medical Rehabilitation Centre (DMRC) at Headley Court, a move that aims to provide them with the best possible care, and is facilitated through a referral system similar to the NHS tertiary referral system.

Four speed enforcement cameras installed on a two-mile stretch of the M4 in Port Talbot, Wales, have resulted in about 125 drivers a day being caught speeding, marking a decrease from the 700 a day during a trial period in the area. While the decrease is welcomed, the Wales Road Casualty Reduction Partnership emphasizes that excessive speed remains a common cause of accidents and fatalities, and their priority is education over enforcement after considering engineering solutions.

A Manchester-born man, previously residing in the Seville area, was arrested in Valladolid, Spain, on suspicion of taking secret photographs of his students and sending explicit images of minor children online. Spanish police found a large number of sexually explicit files involving minors at his residence, including a dedicated folder containing photos of one girl. The authorities are currently working to identify the victims shown in the images.

A seven-year-old sturgeon named Steve, once displayed at World of Water in Romsey, Hampshire, survived a flood and was later found at a nearby car wash. The centre's manager reported the fish, which can retail for up to £1,000, had some scrapes but was otherwise in good spirits, having made a dramatic escape from the flooded facility. The centre has since reopened after the three-week flood closure. Chadwick, another expensive koi carp, also escaped but remains missing.

Chris Rock, the comedian and actor, has filed for divorce from his wife, Malaak, after 19 years of marriage, focusing on their family privacy; they share two daughters, the latest film starring Rock is a comedy about a comedian bystander in his own reality TV wedding.

A collision on the motorway between Tamnamore, Belfast and Enniskillen has caused closures, extensive traffic delays, and police are advising diversions, seeking witnesses, and urging anyone who saw a Honda Civic before the accident to contact them.

The French government has proposed senior diplomat Laurent Stefanini for the role of ambassador to the Vatican, aiming to test Pope Francis' more liberal stance towards homosexuality, but the Vatican has yet to respond or approve the choice.

The Nasdaq fell 2.4%, marking its biggest one-day drop since April 2020, driven by declines in semiconductor, biotech, and other tech stocks, despite a 35% rise in Kraft Foods after it agreed to merge with Heinz, and a 1.6% decline in the Dow Jones and 1.5% decline in the S&P 500. The dollar fell 0.5% against the euro due to a drop in US durable goods orders.

Two underdogs had memorable victories in tennis tournaments: Marketa Vondrousova, the Czech world number 233, moved closer to the top 100 for the first time by beating Estonia's Kontaveit and Barbora Strycova to win a match, while Borna Coric, the 20-year-old Croatian world number 79, saved five match points to clinch his first ATP title over Germany's Philipp Kohlschreiber at the Grand Prix Hassan II in Marrakech.
Stoke City signs Eric Choupo-Moting, a 28-year-old forward with international experience, as their fourth summer acquisition, making his debut in their opening Premier League game against Everton.

A man with cerebral palsy who was 56 and lived in a nursing home in Randalstown, Maine, died last September. The death was initially not treated as a murder case, but in April of this year, the results of an autopsy led to the case being reclassified as potential murder, and a woman is currently being questioned by police.

Heavy rains have resulted in waterlogging on major streets, causing city-wide disruption in Chennai, affecting 80,000 people in neighboring Sri Lanka, and triggering evacuation of at least 10,000 people. The government, army, and disaster response forces are working on rescue efforts, and a relief fund of 5 billion rupees has been announced. The Chief Minister says the excessive rainfall is beyond measures, causing severe flooding and damage.

A McGill's 904 bus caught fire on the A760 Kilbirnie Road near Largs on Saturday, with the driver successfully evacuating all passengers without injury, as mentioned by one grateful passenger whose partially-sighted mother was on board. The road was closed, but it was later reopened after the burnt-out bus was removed.

Notts County's 25-year-old bowler, Jake Ball, is the leading wicket-taker in Division One of the County Championship in 2016 with 12 wickets in two games, including a six-wicket haul in each, demandingly leading the bowling attack alongside Stuart Broad and praised by Mick Newell and Peter M. Read for his impressive form this season.

A memorial stone made of Jersey granite, in memory of 120 men known as "the Jersey Pals" who perished during the Battle of the Somme, was unveiled in Guillemont, France, and a core from its middle, symbolizing a person's heart, will be brought back to Jersey to become part of a monument in Royal Square.

Actor John Boyega, known for his role in Star Wars: The Force Awakens and a former member of Theatre Peckham, expressed his honor to give back to the theatre that nurtured his talent, with theatre's founder Teresa Early emphasizing Boyega's inspiring example for its young members.

In the European Tour event, Thailand's Aphibarnrat holds a one-shot lead with a birdie at the 14th, while Fitzpatrick, who led since day one, matches him with a birdie at the 15th. Donald, former world number one, scores a 65 and is four behind, while Westwood is two shots more back after a 67. Several players are within five shots of the lead, and Dredge, seeking a win since 2006, withdraws due to a viral infection.

In a County Championship match, Middlesex struggled initially losing their openers but a strong third-wicket partnership between Ashton Agar (Voges, 128*) and Dawid Malan (147), setting Middlesex up for a potential win, though poor weather on Tuesday could complicate matters.

A 52-year-old woman died and a 16-year-old boy is critically ill in hospital following an incident on Penilee Road, while police investigation continues and a previously wanted 54-year-old man has been located elsewhere.

The three-bedroom red brick terrace house at 9 Newcastle Road, Wavertree, once lived in by John Lennon from birth to age five, was sold to an anonymous bidder through a bidding war for an undisclosed amount, exceeding its guide price of £150,000 to £250,000, with significant interest from local and international buyers.

A man, Aaron Joseph, 29, denied owning a dog that attacked and resulted in the death of David Ellam, 52, while walking his Yorkshire terrier in Sheepridge, Huddersfield. Joseph also pleaded guilty to possessing cannabis on the same day; the trial has been set for February 5, with hopes for an earlier date.

A body believed to be that of Thomas Bebbington, a 22-year-old man from Shrewsbury, was discovered approximately 10 miles away from the city, following his last sighting entering a river on November 10.
Five-week-old otter cubs, requiring six feeds a day, are currently under care until summer when plans are in place to transition them to an outdoor enclosure, including a pool, and provide live food.

A 33-year-old mother of four named Joanne Thompson was found dead at her Old Mill Court home in Newtownards, and authorities are investigating any potential disturbance at a bonfire on Dakota Avenue on Monday, as well as any activity around her home on Tuesday night and Wednesday morning for possible clues.

A record-breaking number of black-tailed godwits, almost doubling the previous record, spent time on a small island in the Hebrides this spring, with a substantial group found in a field in Kilmoluaig. Some of these birds were identified as having come from countries including France, Portugal, and Spain.

Former Rangers player and coach Tommy Durrant will not return to his role with the first team for the upcoming season, having previously worked with the Under-20 development squad, having held various positions in the youth setup, and serving as first-team coach during Walter Smith's second and Ally McCoist's tenures.
A rare albino deer is reported, estimated to occur once in 100,000 births, generating visitor interest as it adjusts to its new environment.

A 15-year-old boy named Asad Khan from Bradford died three weeks after starting at Beckfoot Upper Heaton School, with his mother alleging he was bullied. During the inquest, it was revealed that Asad had expressed feelings of unsafe and thoughts of skipping school for a long time, and described life as generally hard. The coroner is considering calling the boy who received these comments in person. The inquest will continue next month.

The 1654 coronation ceremony painting, which has been hanging in Rokeby Park, Barnard Castle since 1880, is currently under restoration. Although it's unique and valuable, its origin and painter remain a mystery, with no known valuation, and experts are trying to determine how it ended up in Durham.

Macclesfield Town beat Wrexham 3-0, with goals from Danny Rowe, Mitch Hancox, and Danny Whittaker, placing them seventh in the table, while Wrexham remain 15th. Notable player cardings included Curtis Tilt for Wrexham and Jordan Evans for Macclesfield.

The African Football Confederation (Caf) has agreed a sponsorship deal with French oil and gas company Total, marking Total's takeover from mobile phone company Orange as the headline sponsor for 10 of Caf's competitions. However, the value of the deal has not been disclosed yet.

Spain coach Lopetegui has recalled veterans Diego Costa and Juan Mata, while goalkeeper David de Gea, defenders Sergio Ramos, Dani Carvajal, Gerard Pique, Jordi Alba, Marc Bartra, Cesar Azpilicueta, Javi Martinez, and midfielders Sergi Roberto, Sergio Busquets, Saul Niguez, Koke, Marco Asensio, Lucas Vazquez, Thiago Alcantara, David Silva, and Juan Mata are included in the squad for the World Cup qualifier against Liechtenstein and a friendly with Belgium. Final roster includes three goalkeepers (De Gea, Pepe Reina, Adrian), eight defenders (Ramos, Carvajal, Pique, Alba, Bartra, Azpilicueta, Martinez, and others), six midfielders (Roberto, Busquets, Niguez, Koke, Asensio, Vazquez, Silva, Mata), and four forwards (Paco Alcacer, Nolito, Morata, Vitolo, and Costa). A wildfire, considered deliberate and spanning a 5-kilometer area across the border, is being fought by multiple fire services, with dozens of firefighters on the scene. This incident is one of 435 wildfires reported since early May, and officials are urging the public to stop intentionally setting fires due to the risks to lives, property, and the countryside.

Professional cricketer Boyd Rankin, 31, who appeared in one Test for England in 2014 and played 82 matches for Ireland before switching to England in 2012, has returned to the Irish team, meets eligibility in 2016, and is looking forward to helping Ireland potentially gain Test status, particularly ahead of the World Twenty20 in India.

The Northern Ireland Rare Disease Partnership, initiated by the Patient Client Council, seeks to provide an independent voice for sufferers and their carers, aiming to improve treatment and care for those affected by rare diseases, as exemplified by Jane Stewart and her son Saul who have Spondylo Ephysial Dysplasia. The partnership aims to focus on education, special services, and support for affected families, acting as a voice for those with rare diseases who might otherwise have no means to advocate for themselves.

Gloucester Cathedral plans to open its choral group, which was founded by Henry VIII, to include girls, with the aim of discovering and encouraging talented young singers from diverse backgrounds, and an "open day" has been scheduled for the purpose.

Chelsea winger Pedro, age 29, was hospitalized after sustaining an injury in a 3-0 win in Beijing, suffered a concussion, and will wear a protective mask when he returns to training. The rest of the Chelsea squad has since moved on to Singapore for upcoming games against Bayern Munich and Inter Milan.

Former England cricketer James Taylor (27), who retired due to a heart condition in 2016, is now working with Nottinghamshire and Yorkshire's academies, offering one-day cricket experiences to their batsmen. Meanwhile, former Northants captain David Sales, who scored over 22,000 runs in more than 20 years, will focus on improving the technical aspects of the county's batsmen.

A man was charged with criminal damage, disorderly behavior, and assault on police after an incident on Whiterock Road, which was witnessed by people picking up prescriptions, including children, and is scheduled to appear in Belfast Magistrates Court on 5 December.

A yacht's engine failed a mile north-east of Muck Island on Thursday evening, prompting a volunteer crew from Larne RNLI to launch two lifeboats in good weather conditions, successfully towing the yacht to Carrick Marina, with the incident showcasing the effective cooperation between their inshore and all-weather lifeboats.

In the match between Ipswich and MK Dons, David McGoldrick scored his first goal since August, Brett Pitman and Kane Vincent-Young extended Ipswich's lead, only for Chuks Aneke (Revell) to score twice from the spot and a free-kick, and Jarvis pounded in the winning header for Ipswich. Both managers, Mick McCarthy and Karl Robinson, reflect on an exciting but frustrating game, with MK Dons having a challenging overall season.

A pedestrian bridge collapsed onto a London-bound motorway on August 27, causing a motorcyclist to sustain broken ribs and resulting in the man from Darlington being summoned to court on February 17 for charges of dangerous driving, causing serious injury, and criminal damage to the structure, with the road remaining closed for debris clearance and subsequent Weekend reopening.

A large group organized a flashmob in the style of paparazzi, causing a stampede among holidaymakers in Platja d'Aro, Spain, who mistook selfie sticks for weapons and panicked, resulting in 11 injuries and three hospitalizations. The organizers, German women, have been detained and will face public order charges.

Two individuals, Sindyann Regis and Chevaze Mcgregor, are charged with the murder of a 2-and-a-half-year-old boy named Jeremiah Regis, who was found with over 100 injuries, including a bite to the chest, in Wolverhampton, and died of abdominal peritonitis caused by blunt force trauma; the trial is set to commence on April 25, 2023.

A gorse fire on Woodbury Common in Devon, UK, resulted in multiple cases of smoke inhalation and one hospitalization due to burns. Twenty fire engine crews, aided by a police helicopter, are battling the blaze that has engulfed a vast area, with firefighters remaining on the scene overnight. The nearby Woodbury Park Golf and Country Club was evacuated, and the public was advised to avoid the area due to the smoke.

A 15-year lease has been signed for the Leicester Speedway team's Beaumont Park venue, and there is hope for a new start and a promising future for the team, as further meetings are scheduled to establish the management structure, race night schedule, and other arrangements.

A 50-year-old woman named Elizabeth Bowe was found injured at Bobby Jones Place in St Andrews and died three days later in Ninewells Hospital. Her brother, 51-year-old Charles Gordon, was charged with her murder, made no plea in court, and was remanded in custody. The Police Investigations and Review Commissioner (PIRC) has been ordered to investigate the initial police response before the incident, focusing on the police's handling of the case. A report will be submitted to the Crown Office and Procurator Fiscal Service by the PIRC in due course.

A 29-year-old footballer, Jim O'Brien, has signed a two-year deal with Ross County after a brief loan period last season, with the manager expressing excitement about his potential to help develop younger players and implement his return to Dingwall.

In Division Two cricket, Northants seized early momentum against Durham with regular wickets, dismissing top scorer Michael Richardson, Paul Collingwood, Keaton Jennings, and others for low scores. Despite Durham's bowler Barry McCarthy taking 2-20, Northants ended the day with a deficit of 107 runs, 3 wickets down, while former Derbyshire batsman Chesney Hughes and Max Holden contributed to prevent further losses after early setbacks.

A 19-year-old New Zealander trails by one shot the joint leaders Brooke Henderson and Lee Mi-rim after two rounds at the Sahalee Country Club by two-under, with only five players under par at the halfway stage of the second women's major of the year, including Henderson, Lee, Ko, and Americans Gerina Piller and Brittany Lincicome.

Former footballer Gary McAll, 56, returns for a second stint as part of the Scotland coaching staff, by accepting the position as assistant manager to Gordon Strachan, alongside Mark McGhee, in preparation for the World Cup qualifiers. McAll previously worked with the Scottish national team under Alex McLeish during the Euro 2008 qualification campaign.

The article describes a hockey game where Colin Shields scores for Belfast Giants at 15:52 by a setup from James Desmarais and Steve Saviano. Scott Aarssen equalizes for Braehead Clan at the end of the first period. In the second period, Ryan Martinelli and Mark Garside score for Belfast, followed by Alex Foster and Steve Saviano to establish a 5-1 lead. Belfast have a game in hand on Devils, who won against Coventry Blaze 5-3 on Monday evening. The busy festive period continues with Cardiff vs Blaze on Tuesday, and Giants vs Manchester Storm on Wednesday.

Jordan Spieth, the defending Masters champion, suffered a dramatic collapse on the final day of the tournament, culminating in a quadruple-bogey seven on the par-three 12th. Danny Willett capitalized on this, becoming the first Englishman since Nick Faldo in 1996 to win the event. Faldo, a three-time Masters winner, described Spieth's collapse as a scarring and damaging experience, noting similarities with Greg Norman's collapse in 1996.

The article invites individuals to submit their pictures of England, either through email, social media, or Instagram, with hashtag #englandsbigpicture. Submissions should be from the past week, and the BBC retains the right to use, edit, and publish the images, while the contributors retain the copyright. Contributors should be mindful of their own safety and obey all laws when taking the pictures.

Eye specialist Honey Rose is on trial for gross negligence manslaughter, accused of failing to detect serious swollen optic discs during a routine eye test on Vincent Barker (Vinnie), leading to his death due to a build-up of fluid in his brain. The trial is ongoing.

Food price inflation increased to 4.9% in June, primarily due to rising pork prices, remaining below the target figure of 3.5%, which diminishes the possibility of interest rate cuts in 2013. Amid concerns of a property bubble, analysts anticipate China's monetary policy to stay neutral, with authorities aiming for 7.5% economic growth this year, the slowest rate in 23 years.

Ivorian footballer Cheick Tiote, aged 30, passed away following a collapse during training with Chinese second-tier side Beijing Enterprises on 5 June. His memorial service was attended by friends, family, and former team-mates, with Senegal striker Cisse expressing grief, describing Tiote as a brother. Known for his seven-year stint at Newcastle United, Tiote made over 150 appearances for the club, and had recently joined Beijing Enterprises in February.

In the fifth stage of the race, Peter Sagan of Slovakia won an uphill sprint, while Yates of Orica-Scott dropped out early; Thibaut Pinot moved to second overall, behind leader Nairo Quintana of Colombia, and Geraint Thomas of Team Sky finished fourth on the stage and is now sixth overall, with two stages remaining. The overall standings are led by Nairo Quintana, with Thibaut Pinot, Rohan Dennis, Primoz Roglic, Tom Dumoulin, Geraint Thomas, Rigoberto Urán, Jonathan Castroviejo, Bauke Mollema, and Simon Spilak following closely.
Cuadrilla secures approval for its fracking plans in Lancashire, promising local jobs, investment, and community benefits, but opponents have initiated a legal challenge.

Three 17 and 19-year-old males from north-west London, suspected of planning to travel to Syria, were arrested by Turkish authorities upon their return to the UK, were later released without charge after investigations, and had previously flown from Barcelona, Spain, to Istanbul, coincidentally near where three schoolgirls also went missing and are feared to have joined Islamic State militants in Syria.

A respiratory consultant, Dr. Christopher Davies, criticism a high-cost blackout blind purchased by a matron from Homebase instead of a cheaper option, stating the quote was rejected by the hospital's management. The hospital clarifies the blind met fire and infection control regulations, and NHS England is investigating the situation.

Adam King was instrumental in Swansea City's 2-0 win over Reading in March, and the Swans' development squad clinched the league title with a draw against Wolverhampton Wanderers, achieving 31 wins throughout the 2016-17 season, while the senior team was able to stay in the Premier League despite Hull's relegation due to Crystal Palace's 4-0 victory over them on Sunday.

December 2013 storms damaged a dune system east of Barkby Beach in Prestatyn, with natural re-establishment observed but concerns remain due to narrowness. The Denbighshire council is considering creating a secondary dune system to strengthen defenses, with discussions ongoing with Natural Resources Wales. In Rhyl, a worst-hit area, about 400 homes were evacuated due to flooding from high tides and gale force winds.

South Shields (8th tier of English football), captained by Julio Arca and fresh from a Wembley win, will face Bridlington Town in a FA Cup match streamed live on BBC Sport's digital platforms, with commentary from Conor McNamara and Danny Webber. The game will be accessible on PC, mobile, and connected TV, with audience engagement via #bbcfacup.

Police are investigating a targeted attack on Craigmillar Castle Road, where a 38-year-old man suffered serious, but non-life threatening, facial injuries, and a 49-year-old man did not require medical attention. Police Scotland is asking for witnesses and information about any suspicious behavior or vehicles in the area around the time of the incident.

A 51-year-old woman, Pamela McLaggan, pleaded guilty to manslaughter after the death of 44-year-old Jonathan Baines, known as "Willy," at a house on Ropery Road, Gainsborough, following an outing to Market Rasen races and subsequent pub visits, and is currently in remand, awaiting sentencing on 21 December at Lincoln Crown Court.

A 15-year-old boy was attacked by a couple in their 40s at Patterton station, suffering facial injuries including an eye injury, and lost his mobile phone in the incident. The assault occurred on a 23:05 service between Glasgow Central and Neilston, with witnesses urged to contact British Transport Police if they have relevant information.

A 17-year-old from Dewsbury was questioned under the Terrorism Act in April regarding potential ties to Islamic State, and the West Yorkshire Police are currently investigating him and another teen who disappeared in March, whose families expressed concern and hope for their safe return. Additionally, Hassan Munshi's brother, who is now an adult, was previously arrested and convicted under the Terrorism Act at age 16 for possessing a napalm-making guide on his computer.

The GB ice hockey team, comprising of three Giants' forwards and goalie Stephen Murphy, aims to progress to the final qualifying round for the 2018 Winter Games in PyeongChang by competing against hosts Italy, Netherlands, and Serbia from February 11-14. Notably, seventeen players from the 2015 World Championship (Division 1B) silver medal-winning team have been named, with the GB team facing off against Serie A side Cortina in a two-match 'Olympic Series' while the tournament is ongoing.

Matthew Perry may participate in a tribute to the show's creator, James Burrows, by recording something, but it is not the reunion of Friends that fans have been anticipating, as the main cast is expected to take part. Additionally, Perry is set to appear in a dark comedy play titled The End of Longing in London's West End from February 2 to May 14.

Veteran footballer Jones, who has a history with Manchester United and several other clubs, continued his journey with Burnley last season as they clinched the Championship title, and he began the recent Premier League match against Swansea.

A renowned lawyer from Melbourne's Italian community, who had represented crime bosses accused of various offenses, was murdered, and authorities suspect that local underworld figures may have orchestrated his death due to lingering tensions in the city's criminal landscape.

An Air France 777-200 flight traveling from Paris to Vancouver was diverted to Prestwick, Scotland, due to a slight smell of burning on board, and a second aircraft was sent to transport passengers back to Charles de Gaulle Airport.

The Met Office has issued a severe weather warning, predicting strong winds and heavy rain as Hurricane Gonzalo reaches Britain on Monday night, particularly affecting coastal areas and north-western parts of Wales, with potentially damaging gusts exceeding 55mph inland and up to 70mph by exposed coastal areas, also canceling some Irish Ferries sailings between Holyhead and Dublin due to adverse weather forecasts.

The article discusses concerns about hospital overcrowding, as told by Jenny, who spoke to a doctor in a children's hospital in Sheffield, and shared the experiences of patients Lilly and Jake, who had to wait extended periods due to overcrowding and subsequent wait times to be treated.

A 64-year-old man, Kenneth David Dickie, died from a serious head injury at Rockley Park site in Poole, a 34-year-old man is charged with causing grievous bodily harm, and a 57-year-old woman is arrested and bailed for grievous bodily harm with intent and perverting the course of justice, in relation to Dickie's death.

Former Manchester United forward Federico Macheda remains at Nottingham Forest until the end of the season, having not started a Championship match this season and with the club's pursuit of midfielder Andre Moritz unsuccessful due to contract complications. Meanwhile, Forest midfielder David Vaughan has signed a one-year extension.

The body of missing man Christopher Huxtable, who went missing following a building collapse in February, was found, prompting a guard of honour and offering his family closure, while the families of two other missing men, Ken Cresswell and John Shaw, continue to wait for news.

Bosnia-Herzegovina's international player is aiming for full fitness after a hernia injury but may not start against QPR, while QPR is missing midfielder Jordan Cousins due to a quadricep injury, and on-loan winger Kazenga LuaLua is still a question mark due to an ankle injury. Bristol City seeks a win on Friday against QPR to potentially overtake Forest, Burton, and QPR in the standings.

Luca, an ESA astronaut, embarked on a mission to the International Space Station in 2013, experienced the thrill of two spacewalks, orbited Earth over 2,656 times, and traveled more than 110 million km in total, describing the experience as "absolutely fantastic" and filled with excitement.

The 16-year-old England Knights player, Joe Arundel, who made 44 first-team appearances for his previous club with 16 tries, expressed anticipation and a touch of nervousness about his new challenge at Hull FC, as the club is known for building a culture and winning mentality that aims to foster long-term success, both for Hull FC and the England national team.

Ulster Bank is urgently working to rectify an issue causing payment delays for about 600,000 customers, following an IT problem, after a similar incident in 2012 which led to a large fine for its parent company RBS.
In the 2016 Women's Africa Cup of Nations qualifiers, Tanzania secured a 2-1 victory over Kenya, while Ethiopia defeated Uganda 4-1 in the play-off for third place.

McDonald's Japan is rationing French fries due to a lack of potatoes caused by industrial action at West Coast American ports, importing extra stock to meet demand while limiting servings in their over 3,100 outlets. This shortage comes after a butter supply shortage in recent weeks that affected supermarkets.

The total purse for the upcoming Classic on 3 June will be £1.625m, with Cracksman leading as the favourite after beating Permian in the Derby Trial in April; meanwhile, 1,000-1 outsider Diore Lia is set to race, aiming to generate funds and publicity for Great Ormond Street Children's Hospital at the request of owner-breeder Richard Aylward.

Atletico Madrid's top scorer, Antoine Griezmann, has a haematoma on his left foot, avoiding a potential bone injury, and will miss France's friendly against Ivory Coast for treatment, as Atletico prepares to host Real Madrid in La Liga.

Former Australian rugby league star Willie Mason, who played 15 years with five clubs including Canterbury, where he won a Premiership, and had an international career with 24 tests for the Kangaroos, has joined French Super League club the Dragons after a stint at Manly, with coach Laurent Frayssinous praising his physical and aggressive style and saying he is excited to join the club following the team's difficult start to the season.

The new survey indicates a significant increase in dog feces on UK beaches, particularly in Scotland, raising health concerns due to bacteria present. The Marine Conservation Society emphasizes the positive effort of pet owners in picking up after their dogs, asking them to additionally dispose of the waste in designated dog bins. Despite increased dog waste, overall litter levels decreased this year.

The article discusses a Supreme Court ruling that the government acted unlawfully and unconstitutionally by introducing court fees for employment cases, with these fees being found indirectly discriminatory against women, as they disproportionately prevented them from accessing justice for employment discrimination cases.

In a League match, Wycombe Wanderers secured a hard-fought victory over Dagenham & Redbridge despite having Garry Thompson dismissed. Goals from Paul Hayes, Luke Guttridge (for Dagenham), and Paris Cowan-Hall (Wycombe) proved decisive. Wycombe moved up to sixth place, overtaking Leyton Orient on goal difference, while Dagenham remain in relegation positions, but manager John Still remains optimistic about their future potential.

Bee-eaters, native to southern Europe, successfully bred a second consecutive summer in Low Gelt Quarry, near Brampton, creating nesting tunnels; the RSPB announced that all chicks had hatched and were expected to fledge in the coming weeks.

A man disappeared after his boat capsized on the River Wey in Guildford, and police urge the public not to enter the fast-flowing, flood-warned river if they spot the missing kayaker, instead calling 999 immediately.

A young girl died in a rare and unfortunate accident at Rabat Zoo after a stone thrown by an elephant, possibly out of frustration or boredom, got past the animal's fence and hit her. The incident was caught on video.

MP for North West Durham, Ms. Glass, joins the wave of Labour MP resignations, with Ms. Powell leading the way, stating that the position of current party leader, Mr. Corbyn, has become "untenable." Ms. Glass, with a background in education, enters the shadow cabinet as calls for a leadership election increase, with both Ms. Powell and others expressing lack of confidence in Mr. Corbyn's ability to effectively oppose the government.

Chelsea currently lead the English Premier League with 59 points, with both Tottenham and Manchester United close behind, suggesting a competitive race for the title with six teams in contention. Chelsea face a challenging match against in-form Burnley, emphasizing the need for focus and concentration in every game.

Police and community support officers have implemented a dispersal order in Llangefni, enabling them to force young troublemakers to leave and protect both local residents and the young people themselves from the negative effects of alcohol and related anti-social behavior, with minors potentially being taken home or to a safe place, and repeat offenders facing potential bans or arrests.

Dutch midfielder Marten de Roon, 26, played 33 Premier League games for Middlesbrough after joining for £8.8m in 2016, scoring 5 goals in 36 games, while manager Garry Monk has confirmed interest in Chelsea midfielder Lewis Baker as a potential transfer target.

The Roald Dahl Funny Prize, which honors authors and artists of humorous children's books, will be relaunched in 2016 as part of the author's centenary celebrations, aiming to make it even more impactful.

A 74-year-old convicted white supremacist, Frazier Glenn Miller Jr, also known as Frazier Glenn Cross, was sentenced to death for capital murder and other charges related to last year's hate-motivated attacks on Jewish sites in Kansas. He responded by shouting "heil Hitler" and expressed no remorse, declaring he aimed to kill Jews before dying.

The city council plans to launch a larger self-service bike scheme in April 2017 with 500 bikes positioned at convenient locations including district centers, universities, and other strategic sites, funded through sponsorship income without taxpayer cost. This model is similar to London's 'Boris bikes' system, where bikes are hired and returned using debit or credit cards to any empty docking point.

The article discusses Senegal international Sakho, who has been sidelined due to a back problem all season and is now in the early stages of individual pre-season training following surgery, with several weeks of additional fitness work needed before he can potentially return to competitive play in the Premier League.

The Northern Ireland Residential Property Price Index for Q3 2021 shows an annual increase in property prices by up to 7.3%, with terraced houses having the largest annual rise (7.1%) and the fewest deals being completed in the apartments sector (4% increase). The overall average standardised price is around Â£124,000, with Antrim and Newtownabbey district leading in annual growth and the Ards and North Down district showing the smallest rise. Prices increased by 0.8% compared to Q2 2021.

The article discusses how deliveries of massive wind turbine parts on rural roads in Dumfries and Galloway have resulted in varying outcomes, with one successful passage and another ending in the lorry and its cargo ending up in a ditch.

The Betsi Cadwaladr health board is holding public consultations on possible temporary downgrading of maternity services at Glan Clwyd Hospital due to staffing shortages, with residents expressing concerns about potential increased travel for mothers, while the health board maintains the changes are necessary for safety and has launched a website for public comments.

Mignon du Preez scored a powerful century (116 off 99 balls) while chasing South Africa's commanding total of 272-6, with crucial partnerships from Chloe Tryon and Masabata Klaas' impressive seaming bowling performance contributing to Ireland's defeat for 204, with Du Preez leading a South African recovery after early losses.

British high jumper Lisa Peake, aged 30, aims to break her own Welsh record and secure a place in the Rio Olympics by surpassing her personal best of 4.40m set this year, with British Athletics requiring a qualification standard of 4.50m.
A significant fire at a building site in Llanwern, triggered by a deliberately set blaze involving scrapped railway sleepers, lasted over 10 hours and is now under police investigation.

A charity concert, the Singing Bowl Concert, was held at St. Giles' Cathedral in Edinburgh, organized by Mercy Corps, Nepal Scotland Association, and the city council, to raise funds for those affected by the devastating earthquake in Nepal, with many members of the Nepal Scotland Association losing friends and loved ones in the disaster.

Neil Lennon, Hibernian's head coach, was suspended by UEFA's control, ethics and disciplinary body for acts of violence against a referee during a Europa League qualifying match, which resulted in Hibs losing on penalties. The club is currently appealing the suspension.

A fire broke out 1,100 meters under the sea bed at the ICL UK Boulby mine, causing seven workers to be hospitalized for smoke inhalation. The Health and Safety Executive served an improvement notice to the company, with 11 workers initially unaccounted for, and the incident is currently under investigation. The mine, one of Europe's deepest, employs about 1,100 people and recently underwent layoffs as part of a new business strategy.

Two British tourists, aged 23 and unidentified, were caught and removed from the Unesco World Heritage site, Machu Picchu, for posing naked, under investigation for offenses against morality, but not arrested or charged.

On Friday, 28-year-old Croatia international, Rakitic, is set to sign a new deal with Barcelona, having made 145 appearances since his 2014 transfer from Sevilla, and scoring 23 goals, with a buyout clause at £109m.

A couple in Halstead sustained life-changing injuries in an alleged two-hour torture incident on 26 April, and Kent Police are continuously investigating, providing a detailed description of one suspect, a black man in his 20s, based on victim collaboration.

On July 25-26 at East Kirkcarswell Farm near Dundrennan, the Wickerman Festival will feature Dizzee Rascal as a headliner (the only Scottish festival appearance of the year), along with Martha Reeves and The Vandellas, The Zombies, Big Country, and The Feeling, with further announcements, including the Saturday night headliner, to come.

English rugby players Foden (Saints) and Brown (Quins), both 26, are excelling in the Aviva Premiership, with Foden scoring his third try in two matches as Saints beat Quins 24-3. With England coach Stuart Lancaster naming his squad for the Six Nations on Wednesday, Brown is expected to return for the first time since the tour of New Zealand in 2008. Foden hopes that Saints will contribute multiple players to the England squad for next month's tournament.

A 22-year-old motorcyclist died, and a 10-year-old boy remains in a serious condition following a collision between a KTM motorcycle and a Vauxhall Zafira in Dagenham, with no arrests made; police are seeking witnesses.

Pfizer has agreed to acquire California-based Anacor Pharmaceuticals, with Anacor's eczema cream crisaborole, anticipated to generate $2bn annually if approved by the US FDA, as it addresses a significant unmet need for a large eczema patient population in the US, where 18-25 million people suffer from the condition with few safe and appropriate treatments currently available.

Police were called to Oxlow Lane, Dagenham, at 23:00 BST on Saturday due to a street fight. Officers recovered multiple weapons and cannabis from the crowd, made two arrests (one for possession of an offensive weapon and another for assaulting police), and no one was injured. Insp Jason O'Donohue stated that by recovering the knives, the officers helped prevent another tragedy.
A 23-year-old man from Cardiff was arrested on suspicion of sexual assault after an attack on a 19-year-old woman at Gorsedd Gardens near Cardiff Civic Centre at 04:30 BST on Thursday.

A Scottish Conservative MSP, John Lamont, resigned from his Ettrick, Roxburgh and Berwickshire constituency seat to challenge SNP's Calum Kerr for Westminster, triggering a by-election. The by-election will coincide by-elections for local council and Holyrood representatives in the area.

The EU Commission has announced that countries including the UK, Ireland, France, and Germany can now export beef to Canada, following a decision recognizing the EU's successful measures to eradicate BSE, marking a step forward amid struggling farm sectors due to a Russian import ban and weaker Chinese demand, with a €500m aid package previously announced.

The European Commission is planning to sanction countries on a tax blacklist if they do not comply with changes, as nations have differing views and a previous attempt for a single EU list of tax havens has been blocked. Additionally, the EU has agreed to share information on company beneficial owners and is preparing to crackdown on banks and tax advisers aiding in offshore tax evasion.

Discoveries made during the construction of the West Link in Inverness include Bronze Age burnt mounds, pottery fragments, and remains of kilns used for drying grain, likely relics of a community using heated stones to heat water for cooking, washing wool, or small saunas.

In a League One match, Oldham Athletic secured victory over Southend United, with standout moments including a goal by Main, a saved shot by David Worrall, and misses by Jonathan Forte and Tareiq Holmes-Dennis for Southend, leaving Oldham six points clear of the relegation zone. The match resulted in Oldham consolidating their position while Southend remain in 13th place.

Irish actor Dún Laoghaire native, known for roles in Glenroe, Ballykissangel, and The Secret of Kells, passed away peacefully in hospital, leaving his wife Peggy and their children Saileog, Darach, and Maghnus. He was a fluent Irish speaker and advocate, also having a role in the Hollywood movie Alexander.

Derby City Council, in need of savings of £79m over three years, initially planned to close Moorways Pool to save approximately £350,000 yearly, but after finding savings in back-office areas and restructuring management positions, has committed to keeping it open for a year, while highlighting the potential pool closure if future government funding is not fair. The pool's closure would have left only one other public pool in the city and posed a significant loss in swimming lessons for 1200 young swimmers weekly.

The article reports that children previously held by the militant group Boko Haram have been detained in a military barracks in Maiduguri without proper legal process, as highlighted by human rights groups, with concerns about ongoing detentions of children.

Hearts football club is facing potential goalkeeping issues due to injuries sustained by Alexander (broken cheekbone) and the team's current goalkeeper, Hollis, being a doubt for an upcoming match, with both incidents occurring in the wake of their previous win over Rangers.

Basketball player Chelsey Lee, 26, is under investigation for allegedly fabricating her and her father's birth certificates to qualify as a foreign player in the Women's Korean Basketball League(WKBL), with her team, Bucheon KEB Hana Bank, facing suspension, record annulment, and the scrapping of the extra quota for international players with a Korean ancestry.

The article discusses a new app that assesses Wi-Fi performance and identifies potential sources of interference, while also showcasing statistics from Ofcom's 2015 Connected Nations report, which indicates that while there has been good progress in the availability and use of telecoms services, particularly super-fast broadband, there are still areas in need of improvement, such as rural areas and small businesses.

The article discusses how Manchester United player Paul Pogba used social media to express his feelings after a draw with Liverpool, while teammate Zlatan Ibrahimovic equated social media pressure to the top-tier competitive environment and emphasized his focus on team success rather than individual accolades.

A 73-year-old man discovered a large, car-sized metal object on a river in Salinopolis, Brazil, that was later identified as debris from Europe's Alphasat satellite, launched from the Kourou base in French Guiana last July. The authorities have been contacted to collect the object, and it has been confirmed that the debris is not radioactive. Residents have been advised to report any symptoms of illness.

The article discusses concerns raised by James Purnell that the decriminalization of non-payment of the TV licence fee would lead to an increase in cost for the BBC, potentially reaching £200m, which could result in the suspension of services like BBC Four, CBBC, and CBeebies. The issue is set to be discussed during charter renewal talks in 2017. Former Labour MP John McDonnell has also called for the BBC to reverse its decision to close BBC Three, expressing concerns about potential job losses and reductions in programming quality, and arguing for a licence fee increase that keeps pace with inflation.

Derry City struggles against Finn Harps, conceding two goals to Ryan Curran and David Scully during the match, with Jordan Allan and Rory Patterson managing responses, but ultimately falling short in recovering the deficit, marking Harps' first win over Derry since 1998 and their return to the Premier Division since 2008.

The Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) is mandating that issuers of securities tied to distributed ledger or blockchain technology, such as Initial Coin Offerings (ICOs), must register offers and sales, aiming to protect investors and maintain market integrity.

Operation Anagram, formed by Strathclyde Police in 2006, was instrumental in convicting serial killer Peter Tobin of raping and murdering Angelika Kluk, as well as the murders of Dinah McNicol and Vicky Hamilton. The operation has brought closure to some bereaved families and will continue to investigate any new information regarding Tobin's potential involvement in other unsolved crimes. Tobin is currently serving three life sentences for these crimes.

In the Australian Grand Prix, Ferrari's Sebastian Vettel emerged victorious over Lewis Hamilton, with the latter hoping for a turnaround at the Chinese race as he admits Ferrari did a better job in Melbourne. Hamilton sees the season as exciting due to closeness in racing results, while Vettel acknowledges that beating Mercedes is challenging and they aim to maintain their strong position in future races, acknowledging that Mercedes remains the team to beat.

During the Southwark Crown Court trial, it was reported that Mr Clifford is denying indecent assault charges against a woman in his London office in the 1980s. The woman claims he forced her to perform a sex act and she feared he would "rape or kill" her. In his police interview, Mr Clifford gave a "no comment" response to questions about the incident, including blocking the woman's access to a stairwell and exposing himself. Mr Clifford, who represented several high-profile public figures during his career, will give evidence in court on Monday.

Ospreys coach Steve Tandy expects an intense, physical match in the Pro12 due to the weather conditions, with Nicky Smith available for the game which could help bridge the gap with rivals Scarlets, whose previous match was try-less.

The annual Diwali celebration on Leicester's Belgrave Road, known as the Golden Mile, drew a massive crowd, with fireworks, street art, and stage performances marking the celebration of light over darkness. The event, one of the largest outside India, was not limited to Hindus, Sikhs, or Jains, but attracted people from various backgrounds, fostering a sense of unity and shared joy. Additional city-wide Diwali events included arts and crafts at Newarke Houses Museum and Gardens and shows at Curve theatre. Traffic was restricted on Belgrave Road and Belgrave Flyover during the festivities.

Rosie's Helping Hands, a charity founded in memory of 16-year-old Rosie Ross who was tragically killed in 2001, has raised £350,000 for young people's projects in Aldridge. Her parents, Karen and Ross, have decided to wind down the charity after the last annual Rosie's Walk event, as they feel the 16th anniversary next year will be an emotional milestone, and they no longer wish to be constantly reminded of their loss. The charity has contributed to various projects, including a play area on the children's ward at Walsall Manor Hospital, which greatly improved the environment and helped children cope with their hospital experience.

Macmillan Cancer Support plans to invest £5 million in a new palliative care unit at the Llantrisant site, aiming to provide inpatient, outpatient, and day care for incurable cancer and other conditions, subject to planning approval. The unit, funded in partnership with the Cwm Taf Health Board, would be Macmillan's most significant single investment in Wales and is intended to address current challenges associated with transferring patients between hospitals for tests and treatments. If approved, construction is expected to commence later this year, with the new center potentially opening in late 2018 or early 2019.

The article discusses Wales, particularly North Wales, being ranked 10th in the world by travelers based on a variety of factors such as hospitality, stunning landscapes, and unique experiences. Noteworthy attractions include Surf Snowdonia, Zip World, and the Snowdonia National Park, with the Welsh government expecting an increase in tourists for 2017. The new attractions at these locations will be part of a broader effort to boost the Welsh economy. North Wales was praised for its overall appeal to tourists. Tom Hall, the Editor-in-Chief of Lonely Planet, described North Wales as "a destination that's hard to ignore." Additional locations on the top 10 list include Choquequirao in Peru, Taranaki in New Zealand, the Azores in Portugal, and others.

The Columba Declaration, jointly authored by a Presbyterian Kirk minister and the Church of England's Bishop of Chester, aims to strengthen communication and partnership between the Church of England and the Church of Scotland, recognizing each other formally for the first time. The agreement establishes a 'light touch' contact group, allowing clergy and laypeople to be welcomed into the other Church when moving across the border, while acknowledging each Church's constitutional responsibilities in separate parts of the UK. Both Churches plan to further debate the report over the coming months.

British Army veteran, L/Bdr Parkinson, who was seriously injured in a bomb attack in Afghanistan in 2006, was nominated to carry the Olympic torch due to his inspirational recovery and determination, despite his brain injury taking his speech. Thousands of people have shown support for him, leading to a Facebook issue where he cannot accept more than 5,000 friend requests on his personal page. He has received an overwhelming amount of support, with his posts and emails going through the roof, as well as hundreds of requests to visit places with the torch. Facebook suggests he considers having a page instead of a profile or uses the 'subscribe' feature.

Large quantities of Captagon pills, a stimulant drug commonly consumed in the Middle East, were seized at Beirut's airport, resulting in the detention of five individuals, including a reported Saudi prince, as they prepared to board a private jet bound for Saudi Arabia. This was the largest drug smuggling operation discovered at the airport, and Captagon, which has been linked to fueling conflicts, particularly in Syria, is known for generating substantial revenue.

The Sexual Offences, Exploitation and Child Abuse Command is investigating allegations against Kids Company, a charity founded and run by Camila Batmanghelidjh that provides support to some of the most deprived and vulnerable inner-city children; the charity emphasizes that its priority is the safety of its clients and has robust policies and procedures in place to protect them, reporting any allegations of misconduct to the police if necessary.

The Queen, as she turns 90, is characterized by her cousin Margaret Rhodes as having a ability to imitate the Norfolk brogue and tell amusing stories, even managing an impression of a Scottish accent from her time at Balmoral. She will spend her birthday at Windsor Castle, with gun salutes and Army cadet force beacons at various UK locations.

The UN Agency for Human Settlements report indicates that income inequality in Latin America remains extremely high, with the richest 20% earning on average 20 times more than the poorest 20%. The study shows Guatemala as the country with the widest disparity, while Venezuela is the most equitable. The region is the world's most urbanized, with eight out of 10 people living in cities, and by 2050, nearly nine out of 10 Latin Americans will live in cities. The report suggests that during this period of relative economic stability and slower population growth, Latin American nations should prioritize making city life more equitable. The report also notes a considerable job deficit and a high level of labor informality, particularly affecting young people and women. However, the UN Agency for Human Settlements' Erik Vittrup points to some positive trends, including a reduction in poverty, indigence, and unemployment in urban areas.

A Carmarthenshire Labour councillor, Tegwen Devichand, is under investigation after screenshots showed she shared a post from the far-right group Britain First that called for the death penalty for sex offenders, contrary to her opposition to the death penalty. Additionally, she opposes plans to eliminate English-stream education at a local school, causing controversy within her party and having previously accused Labor members of working with UKIP to undermine school decisions. Dissenting counterparts have criticized her views and she has accused her opponents of a "hate campaign," alleging that a different party member was suspended over the incident on Sunday.

A campaign group led by relatives of British troops killed in Iraq launched a crowdfunding campaign aiming to raise money to seek legal action against key individuals involved in the 2003 invasion, following the Chilcot report which rejected the legal basis for UK military action and criticized the decision-making process. The funding bid received a significant amount of support from the British public, surpassing its initial £50,000 goal within nine hours. The funds will be used to hire legal experts to analyze the report and provide guidance on potential legal action.

Adnan Syed's legal team is reopening his case for the 1999 murder of Hae Min Lee, after new evidence from the Serial podcast regarding mobile phone records and a potential alibi has been allowed by a judge. Asia McClain, a friend who claims to have seen Syed at a library during the time of the suspected crime, could serve as his alibi. The original legal team's failure to present McClain as a witness is one of the key points of contention, with potential prosecutorial misconduct also under scrutiny.

A 16-year-old boy, who previously served custodial sentences for assaults at younger ages, admitted assault and theft at a Dundee party after pulling a machete on a taxi driver, prompting another boy to steal the driver's change. The court deferred sentence until next month for a social work background report.

John Clancy, a Labour councillor for Quinton, was elected as the new leader of Birmingham City Council after five attempts, beating closest rival Penny Holbrook in a ballot by a single vote. Clancy, who has pledged to make smarter financial decisions, improve political openness, provide free school meals for all primary children, and widen access to free school meals, will take office on 1st December. His tenure comes as the council faces scrutiny from a government-appointed independent panel amid ongoing criticism of its management.

In an interview with Empire magazine ahead of the release of "Skyfall", actor Roger Moore discussed his early meetings with director Guy Hamilton and his approach to avoiding deliberate comparisons to Sean Connery in portraying James Bond. Producer Barbara Broccoli also shared insights on Connery revolutionizing the traditional image of a leading man, as well as the significant contributions of dance teacher Yat Malmgren and scriptwriter Terence Young to Connery's performance in the early Bond films.

Witches' marks, carvings believed to provide protection against witches and evil spirits, were prevalent during the period when belief in witchcraft and the supernatural was widespread. These marks, including the "Daisy Wheel" and various religious symbols, are often found in buildings like the Tower of London, the house where Shakespeare was born, or medieval churches. Historic England encourages people to document these findings this Halloween to expand the understanding of such historic symbols and the beliefs associated with them.

The article describes an instance during Prime Minister's Questions where Jeremy Corbyn, the leader of the Labour Party, compared Prime Minister Theresa May's approach to negotiating Brexit with Baldrick from the 1980s BBC TV show Blackadder, due to May noting Sir Tony Robinson, who played Baldrick, was a Labour member. The comparison was meant to suggest that the government's strategy for leaving the European Union is lacking a clear and effective plan.

The Liverpool County Court has ruled that airlines in the UK should pay compensation to passengers for delays in flights, overturning applications by Jet2, Thomas Cook, Ryanair, and WizzAir to delay payments, following EU legislation on flight delay and cancellation compensation.

Jamie Dimon, CEO of JP Morgan, warns that the control of job migration post-Brexit is no longer in the UK's hands as the EU dictates movement of jobs out of London, with France offering incentives to bankers willing to relocate, and HSBC's Stuart Gulliver indicating his willingness to move bankers to Paris while expressing some reservations.

China defends deploying surface-to-air missiles on a disputed island in the South China Sea, claiming it's for self-defense, while the U.S. expresses concern over the escalating militarization in the region and expects to have a serious conversation with China about the issue. Several nations including China, Taiwan, and Vietnam claim territory in the South China Sea, which is also a significant shipping route, leading to growing global concern about potential conflicts.

The study reveals that Adanson's house spider uses its silk draglines to stabilize and brake during jumps, allowing it to land poised and ready to capture prey. This finding could inspire the design of miniature robots with maneuverability similar to the spider.

The Supreme Court ruled that UK ministers are not legally obligated to consult devolved legislatures, including Wales, on the triggering of Article 50, but the ruling leaves open the possibility for the Welsh Assembly to have a vote on the issue, with no veto power, and influencing the UK government to respect the Sewel Convention for the matter.

The Co-op Bank, known for its ethical stance and having four million customers, has announced that its recapitalization plan with existing investors is substantially agreed, aiming to address the bank's struggles to meet Bank of England regulations and the unattractiveness of its pension liabilities to potential investors.

The Swansea tidal lagoon project, worth £1.3bn and seen as a test bed for future schemes, has Tidal Lagoon Power (TLP) disputing the estimated fish mortality rate provided by Natural Resources Wales (NRW). TLP claims NRW's estimates lack a "clear scientific basis" and are not backed by adequate evidence. NRW disagrees with TLP's criticism, stating that the estimates were based on "best available evidence" they have received. The UK government is currently considering a review of the viability of the scheme, with Wales' Environment Secretary expressing desire for clarity on the UK government's position.

The article humorously recounts the most notable blunders, sexist moments, and embarrassing instances from the latest season of a reality business competition show, highlighting unexpectedly outdated choices (hypnotherapist's demands), sexist question choices (Daniel Lassman's board game), navigation mishaps (Sanjay getting lost), dreadful presentations (Solomon's lack of figures), and unsuccessful product pitches (Mark Wright's hacking cough) made by the contestants, offering viewers the satisfaction of thinking they could have done better.

The Home Affairs Select Committee found that the UK's immigration cap, which limits recruitment of non-EU skilled workers, has been counter-productive, leading to increased rejections of nurse applications, and potentially causing a winter crisis in the NHS due to the prioritization of higher-paid jobs.

In Brecon, 20-year-old off-duty soldier Matthew Boyd was fatally attacked outside a bar. The attacker, Jake Vallely, was boasting of being the "hardest man in Brecon" during his seven-hour drinking binge before the incident. Vallely's friend Aaeron Evans was cleared of manslaughter by a jury, as they determined he wasn't present during the attack. The trial was described as shocking by the senior investigating officer, who urged people to avoid violence during nights out, while a tribute for Pte Boyd, who served with the Royal Gibraltar Regiment, praised his loving and carefree nature. Vallely will be sentenced on 8 December, and the family felt that the members of the Brecon community, who showed support during this trial, are the strongest people in town.

The BBC, in collaboration with This Place, has developed a brainwave-reading headset that allows users to select and operate the BBC's iPlayer on-demand platform, potentially benefiting those with disabilities and furthering the use of mind-controlled technology.

The chief inspector of schools, Meilyr Rowlands, stated before the Welsh Assembly's Children, Young People and Education Committee that schools have been inadvertently neglecting higher-performing students due to performance metrics, and that there's a need to focus on elevating the standards for all young people, with changes being made to how schools are measured and the system used for 15-16 year olds.

The unreleased 1981 and 1984 recordings by Johnny Cash, featuring duets with his wife June Carter and friend Waylon Jennings, titled "Out Among the Stars", will be released in March, posthumously. The recordings, featuring 12 tracks, were found gathering dust in a vault in 2012 and have never been released before. They are expected to bolster the already lucrative business for the Cash estate, with Johnny Cash having sold more than 90 million records.

The tribunal ruled that Maria McKeith was unfairly dismissed from her part-time role at the Ardoyne Association for being a primary carer of a disabled daughter, which contradicts the Disability Discrimination Act 1995. The court of appeal dismissed the Ardoyne Association's appeal. McKeith was awarded compensation of £10,000 for injury to feelings, £6,760 for loss of earnings, and £2,126 in interest. Employers are reminded to recognize their obligations under the Disability Discrimination Act, particularly in regard to employees who are themselves disabled or are primary carers of a disabled person.

Scottish midfielder Dorrans, previously at Norwich after spells at West Brom and Livingston, has signed a three-year deal with Rangers, becoming Pedro Caixinha's ninth summer signing for the Ibrox club, whom he has always aspired to play for.

Team Brewster clinched the men's spot for the European Championships by defeating David Murdoch's Olympic silver medallist team 7-2 9-5, while sister Eve Muirhead's rink secured the women's place in a five-game series. Both Muirhead and Glen Muirhead are excited about representing their home country at the event, and Glen's long-term girlfriend Anna Sloan will be returning from injury to play third for the team.

Councillor Pierre Oxley has called a scrutiny meeting regarding a beach defense project, accusing the council of not being clear about the beach composition, while the council's representative maintains they have been transparent and that the meeting is unnecessary.

John Nelms, co-owner of Dundee Football Club, announced plans to submit a land use application for land in Camperdown Park, following a £530,000 operating loss, with the intent of improving and enhancing the club's stadium, which he deems the biggest issue, and potentially furthering Dundee Football Club.

Chris Froome, the Team Sky rider, finished second in the second stage of Criterium du Dauphine, two seconds behind Movistar's Jesus Herrada, while overall leader Alberto Contador remains six seconds ahead of Richie Porte.

The ex-EastEnders star Sian Blake, 43, and her sons, Zachary, 8, and Amon, 4, were found dead in their home on Tuesday, and the case is now being treated as a triple murder inquiry. The police are seeking Arthur Simpson-Kent, the partner of Sian, who has reportedly left the UK and travelled to Ghana. The Met police's handling of the case is being investigated by the IPCC following earlier concerns about Sian's welfare, with significant attempts made to conceal the bodies found in the garden during excavations on Tuesday.

Due to multiple match interruptions, Wimbledon organizers have decided to play tennis matches on the traditional rest day (middle Sunday) for the first time since 2004, with at least eight guaranteed singles' matches to be played, and further details to be released on Saturday.

Dutch manager Dick Advocaat, who steered relegation-threatened Sunderland to safety last season, has decided to leave the club despite signing a new contract, citing a commitment to his wife and characteristically forgoing a financial settlement. His departure leaves Sunderland without a victory in eight league matches, struggling in the Premier League and looking for a sixth manager in four years after a trend of managers saving the Black Cats from relegation only to depart the following season.

The Russian economy is projected to experience a 0.8% GDP decline in the next year following a 0.6% growth in 2014, primarily due to a downturn in energy exports, oil price slump, and Western sanctions; the rouble has lost half its value against the dollar this year, and the government is taking measures to shore up its financial sector and protect bank deposits.

Opposition leader Raila Odinga is challenging the 2017 Kenyan presidential election results in court, accusing the electoral authorities of fraud and rigging, while foreign observers describe the election as free and fair. The international community is urging calm amid fears of potential violence, and Odinga insists this is not a concession but a pursuit for justice for voters and a redemption opportunity for the Supreme Court.

A 60-year-old man dies while scuba diving at Agincourt Reef in Far North Queensland, following CPR attempts; this tragedy occurs after two French tourists died from cardiac arrests while snorkeling at Michaelmas Cay, just a few days prior.

The UK, Scottish governments, and Dundee City Council have collectively agreed on a 3.7 million-pound contract to continue the Dundee-London Stansted route, operated by Loganair, for two more years. The UK Government's contribution is 50% through the Regional Air Connectivity Fund, while the Scottish government and Dundee City Council put in 1.4 million pounds and 400,000 pounds respectively. The route will offer two return flights daily and one on Sunday.

World Wrestling Entertainment (WWE) is launching its video streaming service in China, making its part-sport, part soap-opera content available through a local partnership with PPTV.
