The service aims to tap into China's large population and could potentially capitalize on the success of local stars to compete with established sports. However, industry watchers note the challenge of finding local stars and competing for the same demographic.

Three men, including a police officer, are being questioned by West Midlands Police over allegations of conspiring to pervert the course of justice, providing false information that suggested an officer was to be kidnapped as part of a terrorist plot, leading to a high-alert situation at the force and misconduct charges against the officer.

Ireland defeated Poland in a must-win game, with goals from McKee, Magee, and O'Donoghue giving them a commanding 3-0 lead at half-time. O'Donoghue added a fourth, after which Poland reduced the deficit, but McKee scored again to secure Ireland's victory. Ireland will face Wales in the semi-final of the World League 3, with the winners advancing to the final. France and Scotland will play the other semi-final at the same venue. Ireland's coach, Craig Fulton, was pleased with his team's performance, particularly their improved ball control and pressure on the Polish team, but acknowledged that they could have scored more goals.

A 38-year-old man named Philip Craig was sentenced to life imprisonment with a minimum of 25 years for killing 24-year-old Christopher Laskaris, who had Asperger's Syndrome and bi-polar disorder, in Leeds in November. Craig took possessions, including a TV, games console, and guitars, after Laskaris' body was discovered 13 days later in the flat where the incident occurred. A second man, Dempsey Pattison, who was also charged with the murder, had his case discharged in February.

The police have closed the reinvestigation into the death of former police informant Kester David, and have apologized for their insensitive handling of the case in 2010, including a failure to properly investigate at the time and a catalogue of errors in the initial investigation.

In 2015, football was the most attended sport in the UK with 43.4 million, followed by three horse racing events in the top 10. Rugby union attendances rose to 7.5 million due to the Rugby World Cup. Wimbledon was the most popular individual event, while Formula 1's British Grand Prix had the highest average daily attendance. Horseracing was also among the most-watched sports, and two new events entered the top 10, MotoGP's British Grand Prix and the Badminton Horse Trials. Although attendances were less than the 75 million in 2012 (with Olympics effect), they still rose by 6% overall without one-off events like the Rugby World Cup. Upcoming major UK events in 2016 include UCI Track Cycling World Championships, European Aquatics Championships, and FIH Women's Champions Trophy in hockey.

Beyoncé topped the Forbes list of highest-earning music artists, accumulating an estimated $115 million (£73 million) in 2013-2014, with Taylor Swift following closely in second at $64 million (£40 million), Pink at third with $52 million (£32.5 million), Rihanna in fourth with $48 million (£30 million), and Katy Perry at fifth with $40 million (£25 million). The earnings were calculated from touring, record sales, publishing, merchandise sales, endorsements, and other ventures from June 2013 to June 2014, featuring the release of a surprise, self-titled album and various endorsement deals. Other notable artists who did not make the top 10 include Madonna, Nicki Minaj, and Alicia Keys.

In the article, the Scottish National Party (SNP) claims that it has more support among MPs than Labour leader Jeremy Corbyn, citing the loss of two-thirds of Labour's shadow cabinet and its inability to fill key positions post-election. However, Speaker John Bercow recognizes Labour as the official opposition and their leader as the leader of the opposition for statutory and parliamentary purposes. The SNP has not been able to fill all of the relevant shadow posts to the government, including the shadow Scottish secretary position previously held by Ian Murray.

Villagers in Crickhowell have successfully launched a bid to buy The Corn Exchange, which was initially halted by Punch Taverns, aiming to turn it into independent shops with flats above. If successful, about 180 people will become joint-owners, with enough pledged funds to cover the agreed price of £300,000 plus VAT, though more funds may be needed for refurbishment.

Alliance Trust will continue with a strategic review that may lead to a sale or outsourcing, and RIT Capital has chosen not to make a formal bid for Alliance Trust, withdrawing from the company's takeover and mergers procedures.

Alexis Scott, a 39-year-old Police Community Support Officer, was convicted for tricking long-haul passengers at the North Terminal into believing they had excess cash, profiting about £13,500. Her crime, involving uniform and status misuse, caused a severe breach of public trust, tarnishing the police and the country's international reputation.

The educational platform TrueTube, along with Horrible Histories and various other productions, have been nominated across multiple categories in upcoming Bafta Children's Awards, with TrueTube's works being recognized for their impact on young audiences' media consumption patterns. The winners will be announced on 20 November.

Lady Mary Soames, the last surviving child of Sir Winston Churchill, allocated most of her late father's artwork to the National Trust, Houses of Parliament, and Churchill War Rooms. The paintings include Lady Soames' favorites - Coast Scene near Cannes (1935) and View From a Bathing Hut at the Miami Surf Club, 1946. This artistic legacy was accepted in lieu of inheritance tax and will be displayed in significant locations that reflect Churchill's life, in honor of the 50th anniversary of his death.

An ex-investigator from the ombudsman's office was arrested for allegedly stealing sensitive security documents, which police and MI5 believe could endanger lives. The documents don't relate to any current investigation by the ombudsman's office. The police have launched a criminal investigation and have temporarily halted the sharing of sensitive material with the ombudsman's office until a review of security protocols is conducted. Both the PFNI and Ulster Unionist MP Tom Elliott have voiced concerns about the situation and expressed disappointment in the Police Ombudsman's office.

Phyllis Schlafly, a staunch conservative and outspoken opponent of feminism and abortion, is remembered for her role in blocking the Equal Rights Amendment, her influence on the Republican Party, and her endorsement of Donald Trump, who described her as a patriot and a symbol of strength after her death. Her legacy also includes her fight against Communism and the founding of the conservative group Eagle Forum in 1972.

Professional rugby player Sam Morgan, who can play at full-back or fly-half, has decided to leave Bristol after two seasons to continue his career development in Wales, favoring a move that aligns with his aspiration to play for the Wales national team and capitalize on his full-back skills, with Newport Gwent Dragons showing interest in his services.

The article reports that Mufawaka Alabash and Asem Alfrhad were found not guilty of causing the death of three-year-old Syrian refugee Alan Kurdi through deliberate negligence, but convicted of people smuggling, while the image of Alan lying dead on a Turkish beach focused global attention on the refugee crisis in September. Abdullah, Alan and his family's father, survived but his wife and five-year-old son Galib also drowned in the same boat accident. Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan and European Council President Donald Tusk are due to discuss the migrant crisis, with Tusk proposing the possibility of returning migrants to Turkey who arrive in Greek islands.

Former member of the CIA, Robert Lady, who was sentenced to nine years in jail for his involvement in the 2003 abduction and extraordinary rendition of an Egyptian cleric, had been released and boarded a US-bound flight, according to American officials. This decision was made after his arrest near Panama's border with Costa Rica. His trials in Italy were the first involving the CIA's practice of transferring suspects to countries where torture is permitted, a practice that has been widely condemned by human rights groups.

Scottish airports reported significant increases in passenger numbers for January 2017, with Edinburgh leading the pack at 11.7% growth, most of it coming from international flights. Glasgow Airport, with increases in both domestic and international traffic, also saw a 16.1% surge in international passengers. Aberdeen International Airport, meanwhile, showed its lowest decline in passenger numbers for nearly two years, amid a 7% decrease in helicopter traffic due to bad weather conditions and maintenance recalls. Positive changes are expected in May with Ryanair extending its schedule in Aberdeen and introducing new links to Faro, Riga, and the Faroe Islands.
YouTube has increased the maximum view limit for videos from 2,147,483,647 to 9,223,372,036,854,775,808, after Gangnam Style, the most-watched video, reached the former limit.

England, after losing to West Indies and recovering from a poor performance against Afghanistan, aim to win against Sri Lanka to secure a place in the World Twenty20 semi-finals for the second time since its inception in 2007. The defending champions, Sri Lanka, are struggling with their batting but are still considered a strong team due to their quality spinners, having defeated England in their last T20 match.

Scotland's largest cities, Edinburgh and Glasgow, rank second and third respectively in Britain's most congested cities, with estimated losses of £2.8bn and £2.3bn for Edinburgh and Glasgow respectively over the next decade due to traffic jams. The UK-wide total for wasted time in traffic jams is projected to reach £61.8bn by 2025 if congestion levels persist without intervention, according to a study by Inrix Roadway Analytics. London is reported to have more traffic "pinch points" than any other European city, with the most significant impacts on transportation.

In a friendly match, Norway scored three goals, with standout contributors Elyounoussi, Ruud, and Nordtveit, while Northern Ireland struggled to find their stride and managed only a single goal chance, firmly losing 0-3.

Brussels, Belgium remains on high alert as the city fears potential Paris-style attacks, with numerous armed forces on patrol. Authorities suspect links to the recent Paris attacks, with at least one Paris attacker having lived in Brussels. An arrest warrant has been issued for a suspect named Mohamed Abrini, who was seen with Salah Abdeslam, the current target of an international manhunt, two days before the Paris attacks. The two are believed to have driven a car that was later used in the attacks. Investigations continue, with French President Francois Hollande and US President Barack Obama reaffirming their joint commitment to eradicate IS.

A series of coordinated bombings occurred on March 22, 2016 at Zaventem Airport and Maalbeek metro station in Brussels, leading to 31 deaths and numerous injuries. The Belgian Prime Minister called it a "black day" and urged calmness and solidarity. Both Raqqa-based Islamic State and UK authorities suspect the attacks may be linked to the Paris attacks of November 2015. The US has offered help with the investigation.

Local Green Party councillor Alison Teal has received a legal warning from Sheffield City Council, threatening an injunction for her part in protests against the council's tree felling program. This comes after previous charges against her and 13 others were dropped earlier this year. The council maintains the removal of street trees is lawful and necessary, citing ongoing disruption to tree replacement works, particularly by a small number of protesters. The council supports peaceful protests but has deemed direct action, which deliberately and unlawfully stops works, unacceptable.

In one of the worst whale stranding cases in New Zealand, about 416 pilot whales have beached themselves at Farewell Spit on the South Island, with nearly 300 deaths reported. Local residents and conservation department staff are working tirelessly to refloat the survivors, often forming human chains, while scientists continue to investigate the causes of whale stranding events. Farewell Spit, known for its shallow waters, is often cited as a location that causes navigational errors in whales, leading to such incidents. New Zealand has one of the highest rates of whale and dolphin strandings in the world.

The rugby team Ospreys have signed experienced tighthead prop Brian Mujati, a former player for teams like Lions, Stormers, Racing Metro, Northampton Saints, and Sale, to cover for injuries to Dmitri Arhip and Ma'afu Fia, and to provide additional depth in light of Rhodri Jones' potential involvement in the Six Nations squad and the remaining eight PRO12 games and Challenge Cup quarter-final.

The Gwynedd council proceeds to establish a new Church in Wales campus at Ysgol y Berwyn in Bala, although it faces opposition from community members who have signed a petition against the move. The council assures careful consideration of objections, while the Church in Wales reaffirms its commitment to providing quality education for the area's children and young people. The fate of the project will be discussed at the council's cabinet meeting on 14 February, with the planned opening of the new three-to-19 campus scheduled for September 2018.

According to the article, Oxfordshire County Council proposed a plan to save £100m over five years by merging all services under one organization, while district councils prefer three councils and an elected mayor, with each side accusing the other of prioritizing bureaucracy over service provision. The county council insists the change is necessary due to the necessity of further cuts, while the district councils argue it would be disastrous for urban areas like Oxford. Residents are being consulted before the county council's decision on 14 March.

Edinburgh rugby team, with Dickinson, Nel, and Ford in the starting front row, must win five tough upcoming matches, starting against Newport Gwent Dragons, to have a chance at playoff or top six finish. Per Dickinson, they've struggled with errors and soft tries, and have failed to capitalize on opportunities in recent games.

The Northern Ireland Bat Group is rescuing grounded and injured bats that have been impacted by the poor summer weather, with many young ones found abandoned and in unusual locations. Volunteers like Karen Healy are hand-raising these bats and nursing them back to health before releasing them back into the wild. They emphasize the importance of bats for pest control and debunk misconceptions that they drink blood or are blind.

The Supreme Court is deliberating on whether to expand restrictions on the federal law that prevents gun ownership for individuals convicted of domestic violence, as highlighted by a question from Justice Thomas regarding the potential suspension of constitutional rights due to law violations. This discussion comes weeks after the death of Justice Scalia, which may influence the court's balance of power.

Responsible Travel, a wildlife holiday specialist, has decided to drop several tours involving zoos from its 3,500 trip options, as its CEO, Justin Francis, believes that most animals kept in zoos are not endangered and that the arguments justifying their captivity are outdated.

A 40-year-old woman was arrested on suspicion of murder after police discovered the body of a primary-school-aged child in Faringdon, England. Police have stepped up their presence in the area as a means of providing reassurance, while local residents expressed shock and sadness following the incident. The investigation remains ongoing.

A suspect is accused of breaching the Terrorism Prevention and Investigation Measures (TPim) by not contacting a monitoring company and reporting to a police station in January. This is believed to be the first known such breach, but the Home Office has declined to comment on individual cases. TPims were introduced to replace control orders in 2012 and can impose measures such as curfews, travel restrictions, and communication bans for a maximum of two years. Critics argue that this has weakened public protection against terrorism. The suspect (referred to as BM) appeared in court charged with two counts of breaching TPim provisions. A plea and case management hearing was scheduled for 2 July, and the suspect was granted unconditional bail, with the TPim restrictions remaining in place. The trial date was not set.

Qualcomm, the major supplier of chips for smartphones, has agreed to lower royalty rates on patents in China's mobile phone market, a move that could benefit domestic companies like Xiaomi and Huawei, following a ruling that Qualcomm violated China's anti-monopoly law. This adjustment is expected to increase profit and revenue for Qualcomm, with the company stating that it is pleased with the resolution as it removes uncertainty surrounding its business in China.

In the article, it is detailed that Michelle Mellotte, a former doctor, was found guilty of fraud by abusing her role by taking £10,000 from a patient with Alzheimer's, and was subsequently sentenced to a suspended prison term, suspended from the medical register, and is no longer able to practice as a doctor in the UK. The decision was made by the Medical Practitioners Tribunal Service in Manchester.

A nearly complete male skeleton, aged between 30 and 49, was found at the bottom of an embankment near the M54 motorway in Shropshire, UK, around 2-3 years ago. The remains were wearing contemporary clothing and investigators are unable to rule out potential criminal activity, as they continue to investigate the cause of death.

The archaeological discovery of a 30m square of megaliths, previously hidden and buried, inside the colossal Avebury stone circle in England, is thought to be one of the site's earliest structures, possibly dating back to Neolithic times, and is believed to commemorate the ancestral house of the first people who lived in Avebury.

The article discusses an opposition to a parking scheme proposal in Reading by hospital staff and residents, arguing that the implementation of pay and display meters could exacerbate parking pressures around the hospital and university areas, thus presenting challenges for staff, patients, and local residents.

A 21-year-old US Navy member, Petty Officer Aimee Mejia, was involved in a drink-driving accident in Okinawa, injuring two people, which has intensified local criticism of the U.S. military presence there. In response, the Navy has imposed stricter alcohol restrictions and will prohibit service members from drinking, on or off base, until further training is completed to ensure understanding of the impact of responsible behavior.

In the tri-Series, the Lions team, coached by former England captain flower, achieved resounding victories against Pakistan A and Sri Lanka A twice each, with several high-scoring performances by players, notably the unbeaten 220 of Duckett and 171 of Bell-Drummond, the 9th and 8th highest List A scores respectively. The exceptional performances were noted by Flower, who suggested these young upcoming players could have successful international careers.

Colombia's peace talks with the FARC rebels, mediated by Cuba and Norway, are resuming on 10 December following the release of three hostages. The discussions will focus on de-escalating the conflict and addressing victim's family concerns. Parties plan to set up a permanent crisis resolution system, with further talks scheduled around mid-January. The ongoing negotiations aim to end a 50-year conflict that has claimed over 220,000 lives.

The Save Oxfordshire Children's Centres Campaign led a protest against Oxfordshire County Council's plan to close 44 children's centers and replace them with eight, aiming to save £8m. Former Prime Minister David Cameron was invited to join the protest, and an open letter was sent to him expressing disappointment with government funding cuts. The government responded by stating there is room for "sensible savings" in local government.

A controversial sandcastle depicting a murder victim in Police tape, created by Devon and Cornwall Police at a family beach event, was crowned winner but received criticism for perceived poor taste and sexual stereotyping, with some defending it as a source of humor.

Slade, Leyton Orient's football manager, discusses a proposed shift in the club's structure due to a new owner's takeover, emphasizing his focus on football matters and the need for improved team performance, while noting the learning curve involved for both parties. The goal is to build on the progress made towards the Championship, with anticipation of attracting quality players to strengthen the squad.

Tyrrell Hatton secured a spot at the USPGA Championship, booked a place at The Open Championship for the fifth time in six years, and earned his largest career payday at the Scottish Open, despite finishing a shot behind the victorious Swede Alex Noren. Hatton remains optimistic about his performance and aims to make it through to the weekend at The Open.

The 10-year-old Irish-bred horse Many Clouds, known for his successful races including the Cotswold Chase and the Hennessy Gold Cup, suffered a severe pulmonary haemorrhage and died after a race, despite having no significant underlying health issues, prompting questions about possible links to his previous condition of overheating and calls for further investigation into preventing such incidents in racing horses.

A woman testified in Sheffield Crown Court that she was 12 when she was picked up from a children's home, abused, and taken to Blackpool where she was raped and forced to work in a restaurant, all of which is alleged to have been orchestrated by Basharat Hussain, who along with six others is on trial for child abuse in Rotherham. The witnesses claims to have met Mr Hussain and denies that she has never met him during cross-examination. The trial continues.

A 32-year-old racer, Franck Petricola, tragically lost his life after making his comeback at the TT following a serious accident at the North West 200 in 2014, marking the 141st fatality at the races. Organizers and the road racing community express sympathy to his family and friends, with an investigation launched following the incident. Petricola had displayed extraordinary resilience after suffering multiple fractures and a head injury during a practice crash at the North West 200 in 2014 and had made a full recovery to compete just last month.

The Honda Racing team has decided not to let Martin compete in the upcoming event due to his crash at the Isle of Man TT in June and mechanical issues this year, but the race is still anticipated to have strong performances from top racers such as Peter Hickman, Michael Dunlop, and Dean Harrison, with a wide-open field for potential winners.

President Barack Obama has declared a disaster area in Louisiana due to unprecedented historic floods caused by torrential rain, affecting more than 20,000 people who have needed rescue, with over 8,000 to 10,000 people in shelters, and many still stranded in their homes, amid reports of snakes and blocked streets. The floods have resulted in severe damage, with numerous rivers overflowing, and have been compared to the 2005 Hurricane Katrina disaster in terms of its impact.

In the article, US Soccer settles a lawsuit filed by parents on behalf of young soccer players who accused governing bodies, including Fifa and the California Youth Soccer Association, of negligence in addressing concussions. In the settlement, US Soccer commits to limiting heading in practice for children aged 11-13, implementing modifications to concussion substitution rules, and establishing requirements for players in youth national teams and the development academy. The Football Association in England has also announced new guidelines for managing and treating suspected head injuries, with a focus on identifying the long-term effects of head injuries on the brain.

Former president Nicolas Sarkozy was not aware of the falsification of 11 million euros worth of invoices during his 2012 campaign, according to a deputy director of his campaign Jerome Lavrilleux. The UMP party, facing growing allegations of financial mismanagement and potential wrongdoing, with its chairman Jean-Francois Cope and the founder of the events company Bygmalion, Batien Millot, also denying knowledge of the actions taken. The scandal, if proven, could impact Sarkozy's potential re-election bid and complicate UMP's leadership.

The Council of Mortgage Lenders (CML) reported a decrease in home repossessions for the second quarter of the year, with 2,500 homes repossessed compared to 3,000 in the previous quarter and 5,400 in the same quarter last year. This drop was attributed to low interest rates, but the CML urged homeowners to prepare for future interest rate increases. The number of homeowners in arrears also declined. However, the number of tenants evicted by landlords increased by 4% from the same period last year, with Shelter attributing this to ongoing rent rises and welfare cuts.

The article describes that Coventry city accepted 105 Syrian refugees from October to March under the government's expanded resettlement program, while only three refugees were settled in Kingston upon Thames and Mid Sussex. The UKIP MEP, James Carver, argued it was unfair for Coventry to take more refugees than other councils, and expressed concerns about the pressure it might put on local services. On the other hand, the Home Office spokesman and Coventry City Council deputy leader Abdul Khan defended the resettlement efforts, stating that Coventry had accepted cases with significant medical needs and families affected by the violence in Syria, which is the right thing to do.

Brazil's president, Ms. Rousseff, declares her confidence in organizing a safe and successful Olympic Games in 2016, with the Olympic torch relay starting in May and passing through 300 Brazilian cities before culminating at Rio's Maracana stadium at the opening ceremony. She also allays concerns over security, delays, and water pollution, insisting they will not pose significant issues.

Italian Prime Minister Matteo Renzi's reform guarantees a majority of seats to the party that wins the most votes in an election, seeking to end the country's legacy of unstable governments and political instability. The measure, despite concerns over consolidation of power and potential restrictions on voter choice, has been approved and is expected to come into force next year. Critics, including opposition parties, have boycotted the vote, labeling it a "very ugly day for our country's democracy."

The 20-year-old Ajax player Abdelhak Nouri suffered severe brain damage and the chances of recovery are negligible due to a lack of oxygen supply during a game against Werder Bremen, according to a club statement.

Swansea earned a crucial victory after falling behind against Aston Villa, with Gylfi Sigurdsson's free-kick and Andre Ayew's late goal turning the match around. The win, while difficult, provides a boost to Swansea's morale and offers added confidence ahead of their Arsenal game. Sigurdsson emphasized the team's focus on meeting their self-set targets, despite recent struggles in performance.

Mani Dad, a boy living with his Polish mother Leyla Dad in Kielce, Poland, is believed to be with his British father Zayn Dean in the UK. Leyla launching family court proceedings, has asked Costa coffee shops customers to look out for Mani and his father as he frequented these places. She believes they may be residing in a village, with Zayn's potential links to various UK locations like Bolton, Bradford, Birmingham, Luton, Bedfordshire, Essex, and London. The family had previously lived in Kettering, Northamptonshire, and Bedford, and Leyla is urgently seeking to find and reunite with her son.

U.S. authorities have changed travel rules for individuals with dual citizenship from certain countries, including Iran, under a visa waiver program; the new rules were implemented with unclear guidance, leading to confusion and frustration for some travelers, such as BBC Persian service presenter Rana Rahimpour.

Sky is addressing capacity issues at telephone exchanges in certain areas, which have been exacerbated by the launch of Sky Go Extra and a high rate of new customer additions, causing slow internet speeds for some subscribers, particularly in Doncaster, North Wales, and Bristol. Less than 5% of the service's broadband customer base is affected, and Sky is working to add new capacity to those exchanges as quickly as possible. However, the firm has attracted subscribers who download significantly more data than the average UK broadband user, contributing to the network strain.

A Liverpool-based gang, including Joseph McHale, Kevin Schruyers, and Robin Vaughan, were convicted in Scotland for blowups and thefts from ATMs in several locations, stealing over £133,000, and attempting to break into an ATM in Mintlaw. The investigation pointed to Liverpool after Scottish banknotes with signs of dye started circulating in the Mersey area.

The Scottish Government is set to implement mobile phone signal interference technology in two prison sites, HMP Shotts and Glenochil, with the aim to combat the use of contraband phones and associated criminal activities such as drug supply, organized crime, and harassment, as it has been illegal for prisoners to possess mobile phones since 2010. The new policy is scheduled to be operational in a matter of weeks.

Former French President Francois Hollande participated in a ceremony marking 70 years since the Allied liberation of Nazi camps, emphasizing the importance of historical knowledge to prevent future atrocities. Notably, the camps included Natzweiler-Struthof in Alsace, where most inmates were French resistance fighters but also Jews and gypsies; Bergen-Belsen in Germany, associated with Anne Frank's tragic demise; and Jasenovac in Croatia, site of an escape attempt by about 600 inmates, 80-90 of whom survived. The ceremonies coincided with ongoing discussions about attacks on both Jews and Muslims in France, and the president of the World Jewish Congress, Ronald Lauder, addressed the harrowing images and experiences from these concentration camps.

Actor Johnny Depp, 52, and his wife, Amber Heard, 30, have filed for divorce after 15 months of marriage, citing irreconcilable differences; the divorce comes amidst a legal case in Australia over Heard illegally importing two dogs, a spat that led to accusations and insults from both parties, and most recently occurred days following Depp's mother's death.

The Maersk Tigris, a Marshall Islands-flagged ship in international shipping lanes, remains anchored off Iran's coast with 24 crew members after being seized by Iranian authorities, allegedly due to a private Iranian company's complaint about debts. The vessel is carrying commercial goods but no military equipment, and a distress call from the ship was picked up by the US Navy, prompting them to send a destroyer and a reconnaissance plane to the area to monitor the situation. US officials have labeled the Iranian patrol vessels' actions as "inappropriate."

The article summarizes that a family member of Seren Bernard, a 14-year-old who took her own life in 2012 while in foster care in Pembrokeshire, is seeking the full report of a Serious Case Review but the Pembrokeshire council cannot disclose it due to legal reasons. The summary of the report indicates that Seren had previously attempted suicide, but in the days prior to her death, her mood had lifted and there was no indication she was contemplating suicide. The family member expresses frustration and a sense of trauma, as the report's contents leave many questions unanswered and hinders potential learning from the case.

In the Super League match between Leigh and Salford, Leigh dominated from the start, taking an impressive 18-0 lead into half-time with standout performances from Gregg McNally and Atelea Vea. Despite a drop-goal from Josh Drinkwater in the second half, Salford struggled with Leigh's physicality and disciplined play, slipping to a fifth defeat in six games, missing out on third place and dropping to fourth. Leigh's coach Neil Jukes was pleased with his team's performance, citing their game management, defensive effort, and minimal penalties as key factors in their victory. Salford coach Ian Watson was disappointed with his team's performance, blaming a dip in intensity since securing a top-eight finish and urging his team to rediscover their earlier-season hunger and attitude.

Paul Allen, a tech tycoon, is planning to develop a massive aircraft names Stratolaunch Systems, which aims to put unmanned rockets into orbit, eventually undertaking manned missions. The aircraft, powered by six 747 jumbo jet engines and boasting a 385ft wingspan, will drop rockets into space, offering more launch flexibility and minimizing weather constraints. Construction of a hangar in California's Mojave Desert is already underway, and the first test flights are scheduled to begin in 2016.

In a cricket match, Lancashire set a challenging target of 365 for Derbyshire after Tom Taylor took the key wicket of Alviro Petersen but Ashwell Prince and Steven Croft put on a crucial 160-run partnership. Despite a strong comeback by Derbyshire's openers Ben Slater and Billy Godleman falling to Peter Siddle and Tom Bailey, wicketkeeper Alex Davies (89) had a career-best innings, while Derbyshire ended the day on 27-2, finding the high score needed for victory exceedingly difficult. Both sides expressed confidence in their ability to win, with Davies and Taylor acknowledging the importance of maintaining partnerships and bowling well for the remainder of the match.

In his last show, American satirist Jon Stewart, known for his influential content on The Daily Show, was bid farewell by a host of famous guests including Bruce Springsteen, and prominent figures like US Secretary of State John Kerry and Senator John McCain. The show, a prominent news source for young Americans, is being handed over to South African comedian Trevor Noah. Fans paid tribute with the hashtag #JonVoyage, with some instances like McCain's video message possibly marking a moment of gentler banter, as Stewart had once mockingly used a puppet resembling McCain.

In the article, it is mentioned that Forest, a four-time cup winner and two-time European Cup winner, will begin their quest in the cup competition to secure a spot in the Europa League, starting at Doncaster on Tuesday, while their goalkeeper Dorus de Vries is expected to recover from an injury in a few weeks.

The Arches, a nightclub and cultural venue in Glasgow, has gone into administration due to a 50% reduction in revenue following a midnight closing time imposed due to drug abuse and disorder, putting 130 jobs at risk. The Scottish Government is working with Creative Scotland, Glasgow Life, and Glasgow City Council to explore options for the future of the venue, offering support to potentially affected staff through the Partnership Action for Continuing Employment (Pace) initiative.

A senior IRA member from the 1970s, Ivor Bell, was arrested for aiding and abetting murder and IRA membership, as he was part of a delegation that held secret talks with the British government, including Gerry Adams and Martin McGuinness. Jean McConville, one of the "Disappeared" (victims abducted, murdered, and secretly buried by republicans during the Troubles), was kidnapped, falsely accused of being an informer, and her body was found in 2003. Seven of the 16 listed Disappeared remain unidentified.

Wigan Warriors overcame a 12-men disadvantage after Ben Flower's red card, scoring 21 unanswered points to secure a victory, while their hopes for the League Leaders' Shield are slim. They aim to clinch a home semi-final by winning next week's match against Catalans Dragons. Warrington only needs a draw to win the first piece of Super League silverware this season. If Wigan reaches the final for a fourth consecutive year, they may be without Flower due to his red card incident.

The Yorkshire Sculpture Park attracts record numbers of visitors (100,000 in September vs 37,000 last year) due to the installation of the art piece, Wave, consisting of 5,800 ceramic poppies, marking 100 years since the start of World War One. The sculpture, a part of a nationwide tour, is expected to draw more than half a million visitors this year.

A severe flood warning on the A361 between East Lyng and Burrowbridge was lifted on 10 March after inspection and reopening, with temporary traffic lights installed due to residual water. The road was cleared of debris, including fallen trees and used sandbags, starting on Monday. However, a road closure on the A372 Langport Road remains for the removal of flood pumps, with the process starting Monday, expected to last up to four days. The Environment Agency will continue removing the pumps, with improving weather conditions necessitating their removal.

The Subaru telescope's observation points to an icy body, V774104, being around 15.5 billion kilometers from the Sun, making it more distant than even Pluto. Preliminary estimates suggest it could be 500-1,000 kilometers across, but further studies are needed to understand its orbit. The discovery was made by a team led by Scott Sheppard and Chad Trujillo, who specialize in finding Solar System outliers. The currently recognized most distant object is Eris, which moves between 5.7 billion km and 14.6 billion km from the Sun. The discovery was announced at the 47th annual meeting of the American Astronomical Society's Division for Planetary Sciences.

Ashley Yates, a headteacher at The Tynings Primary School in Staple Hill, admitted to making indecent images of children and voyeurism, using a spy pen to record pupils and staff. Police have identified additional adult victims, offering support to them. Yates is remanded in custody until August 9.

The article discusses the victory of the British rowing team Helen Glover and Heather Stanning in the women's pair event at the Rio Olympics, defending their title from the 2012 London Games. The pair, unbeaten in 39 races over the past five years, finished 1.2 seconds ahead of New Zealand, with Denmark in third place. Their win was considered particularly significant as they successfully defended their Olympic title, with Stanning stating that this victory meant even more to them than their previous success in London.

Steve from CBBC's Deadly 60, and his Strictly Come Dancing partner Ola, have faced allegations of bullying, which they've dismissed. Ola acknowledges the public's belief in the claims despite their denial, finding it difficult after being on the show for nine years and suddenly being named. They chose to remain unified, continuing to dance, and have found the recent media attention a significant learning experience for Steve. The pair were voted off the competition over the weekend. They encourage those affected by bullying to seek help, with resources available on the BBC Radio 1 website.

Inflation decreased to 2.6% in June, causing the British pound to fall against the dollar and euro, but initially boosting the FTSE 100 due to the weaker pound strengthening the value of overseas earnings of multinational companies in the index; however, the fall in Royal Mail shares offset this increase, as their revenues rose but letter delivery volumes decreased further.

Actress Vicky McClure, who has a tram named after her in her hometown Nottingham, shared a humorous anecdote on The Graham Norton Show about an incident in 2015 where she and her mother were mistakenly thrown off a tram they were given a free ride on, after being told they could have one following the tram's unveiling ceremony. Nottingham Express Transit, which manages the network, called it an "unfortunate misunderstanding."

The inquest into the death of 14-year-old Alice Gross in the River Brent, west London in 2014, will examine if government and police failures contributed to her death and investigate why Latvian murder convict Arnis Zalkalns, the prime suspect in Alice's death, was allowed to live unchecked in the UK. Alice's family is seeking to establish the robustness of systems for monitoring foreign offenders and cross-border information sharing, expressing dismay over the lack of monitoring of Zalkalns, whom they believe should not have been allowed to re-offend. Alice, described as lively, popular, witty, sharp, and academic, went missing in August 2014 and her body was found a month later, with indications of sexual assault and asphyxiation. Zalkalns, who was convicted of murdering his wife in Latvia in 1998, would have been charged with Alice's murder had he not died.

The Local Data Company and University of Stirling's research revealed a decrease in the average retail vacancy rate in Scotland from 14.5% to 13.7%, with East Kilbride having the highest vacancy rate (33%) and Inverurie the lowest (1%). Over 40% of empty shops have been vacant for more than three years. The most improved towns include Anstruther, Clydebank, Dumfries, Inverkeithing, Lochgelly, Peterhead, and Pitlochry, while five towns have maintained rates under 6% for three years. Conversely, five towns have rates above 22% for the same duration. The report highlights the growing presence of leisure businesses, as well as the significant proportion of charity shops in certain areas, with Aberdeen having the highest percent in a city and Penicuik in the highest percent in a town. Matthew Hopkinson emphasized the implications of 40% of vacant units being vacant for over three years as a major barrier to healthy communities.

Rory McWhirter, of Edinburgh, deceitfully claimed tax credits, child benefits, and a Sure Start maternity grant after fabricating multiple false births using stolen identity details and forged marriage certificates, having previously admitted fraud. His scheme, though elaborate, was discovered when he was recognized by staff at an Aberdeen registry office and found to have returned to a location of an early false birth registration. Despite earning a significant income, his solicitor argued for a lenient sentence due to financial obligations and failed businesses, stating the scheme was an effort to avoid seeking help from his family. However, Sheriff Alastair Carmichael deemed the fraud a serious attack on the public purse, the integrity of the birth, death, and marriage system, and the working tax credit, child benefit, and maternity grants system, and sentenced McWhirter to imprisonment.

Authorities are attempting to demolish Awamiya's old quarter, a predominantly Shia area, allegedly due to militant activity, sparking clashes that have resulted in several deaths and accusations of random firing towards homes and cars by the security forces. Residents complain of discrimination, power cuts, and lack of basic resources, with some seeking accommodation in nearby towns. The unrest has historical roots in the Shia region around the city of Qatif, with tensions escalating since the 2011 Arab Spring and the 2016 execution of the prominent Shia cleric Nimr al-Nimr.

The article discusses the struggles of young people, like Donna Rennie and Marc Young, to find employment, and their frustrations with the political system in Belfast, particularly the perceived focus on elections and personal gains over addressing youth unemployment and related issues such as drug reform and better health care.

In Barnet, Andrew Travers stepped down as chief executive after a major error at the EU referendum in June 2016, where voters were initially unable to vote due to missing names on poll lists; an independent investigation has been launched, with interim leadership by John Hooton, and the results are under review.

Manager Neil Warnock has provided midfielder Peter Whittingham time to consider a new contract offer, stressing that respect is due to the veteran player who recently celebrated ten years at the club, while making it clear that Emyr Huws and Stuart O'Keefe are not part of his long-term plans.

The BBC and BuzzFeed News investigation revealed suspected match-fixing in elite tennis, with a tennis representative stating that if found guilty, players should be banned permanently, and suggesting additional funding for the Tennis Integrity Unit to combat such activities. However, the representative expressed no knowledge of match-fixing at the Australian Open where he is currently playing.

A 60-year-old man, reportedly a customer, entered a bank on Bristol Road South in Northfield, produced a firearm but made no threats or demands, leading to a hostage situation involving a female staff member. The man surrendered to police, was taken to hospital, and is expected to be questioned for suspected firearms offenses. The incident did not harm any customers or additional staff members.

Mohammed Ali, a computer software programmer from Liverpool, is on trial for attempting to illegally possess a deadly toxin (ricin) after being deceived by undercover FBI agents on the dark net, which he used to order the substance inspired by the TV series Breaking Bad. He has denied the charge and displays traits of Asperger's syndrome.

Newport County AFC, tenants of Rodney Parade stadium, are under criticism from dragons coach Westley for pitch issues, with CEO Davies defending the club's commitment to fixing the problem amid concerns about value for money in the leasing deal.

The Aviva UK Health report reveals that a significant majority (69%) of those surveyed have worked while unwell, with fears of a backlog of work upon their return, while only a fraction (23%) admitted to being absent when healthy. This tendency toward "presenteeism" could potentially harm business performance due to decreased productivity and morale.

The Bank of England kept interest rates unchanged and adjusted its 2017 growth forecast downward, while the FTSE 100 closed almost flat with positive contributions from mining stocks; but Fresnillo, Randgold Resources, and Antofagasta rallied, while Hikma plummeted due to a delayed US approval for a new drug and a potential low likelihood of approval this year; Centrica, British Gas owner, plunged due to regulatory concerns and a potential price war, and BT fell due to a decline in annual profits.

Russian hacker Roman Seleznev, son of a Russian MP, was found guilty of running a hacking scheme from 2008 to 2014 that targeted US pizza chains in Washington state, stealing and selling nearly 3 million credit card numbers, and was sentenced to face a mandatory four-year jail term starting 2nd December. His lawyers plan to appeal, citing his "illegal arrest" in 2014 and the use of evidence from a corrupted laptop seized during the arrest.

The article states that in response to questions about alleged tapes of his conversations with former FBI Director James Comey, President Trump claimed on Twitter that he does not have any such recordings. This claim comes after Comey confirmed that Trump had requested Flynn investigation be dropped and asked for loyalty, and following reports of a private meeting where Trump had asked Comey to let Flynn go amid allegations of Russian meddling in the election.

Liberty, led by Sanjeev Gupta, has expressed a bid intention for the Tata Steel assets, with potential financial backing from Macquarie Bank. The firm has a focus on recycling scrap metal and has recently acquired Tata Steel plants in Lanarkshire. The government is prepared to support any successful bid with a 25% stake and significant financing. Tata Steel has not firmly set a deadline for a sale but is under financial strain and wants to avoid prolonging uncertainty for employees and stakeholders.

Local councils in the East Midlands region are considering a proposal to extend the Nottingham tram service to East Midlands Airport and the proposed HS2 station at Toton, as part of a "priority project" in devolution negotiations. The Light Rail Transit Association supports the idea, claiming it would efficiently move passengers to Derby and Nottingham. The cost of the project, estimated at £20m per mile of track, was not discussed in the document. Other projects supported by the local enterprise partnership include unspecified transport interventions to boost regional growth potential.

Ronnie O'Sullivan, the world number six and five-time world champion, won the Masters tournament with a 10-1 victory over Barry Hawkins. Despite returning to the game recently after a long break, and battling a bad back, O'Sullivan feels his adjustment of his game strategy, particularly by adding more power, has helped him remain competitive with younger players, and winning the tournament has boosted his self-belief and confidence ahead of the World Championship in April.

A devastating storm swept across Poland, killing six people, damaging thousands of homes, and devastating over 45,000 hectares of forest, with particularly heavy damage in Torun, Gdansk, and Poznan. The disaster is being called the worst forestry disaster in Poland and potentially all of Europe. The storm comes after the Polish government has faced criticism for logging in the Bialowieza forest, a Unesco World Heritage site, with the European Court of Justice ordering a halt to large-scale logging there last month.

Singer Enrique Iglesias had to undergo additional reconstructive surgery after injuring his hand while attempting to grab a drone camera at a concert, and is expected to take several weeks to recover before resuming his tour on July 3 in Mexico City.

Leeds Rhinos dominated a disjointed Warrington Wire, winning 34-0 with tries from Matt Parcell (3), Joel Moon, Jamie Jones-Buchanan, and Rob Burrow, with Parcell particularly impressive, while Warrington were held scoreless for the first time since April 2016. Leeds' head coach Brian McDermott felt his team was clinical, but recognized that Warrington is not playing at their full potential, while Warrington's head coach Tony Smith was disappointed with his team's execution and ball handling.

William (Plum) Smith, a central figure in the 1994 ceasefire of loyalist paramilitary groups, spent ten years in prison for a 1972 shooting, became a member of the PUP, chaired a press conference for the Combined Loyalist Military Command, served as chairman of the PUP, and was part of the party's negotiation team during the Good Friday Agreement. He is remembered for his intelligence, political left-leaning, advocacy for working-class people, and efforts to bridge divisions with traditional enemies, as noted by fellow political leaders upon his death.

Mrs. Olive Cooke, a 92-year-old resident of Bristol, has been a dedicated poppy collector for the Royal British Legion for over 75 years, a role that took on great personal significance after her husband was killed in action during World War II. Known for her dedication and impact, she is recognized as "one of our longest-standing poppy collectors" and a "most-valued poppy collector" by the RBL.

Shimon Peres, a key Israeli politician present at the country's birth in 1948, who served as prime minister twice, president, and played a significant role in peace negotiations with the Palestinians, winning the Nobel Peace Prize in 1994, died after suffering a major stroke two weeks earlier.

The BBC report reveals that Queen's University staff expressed low satisfaction with leadership and direction in a major survey, with only 29% of respondents agreeing that senior leaders provided effective leadership. However, staff were more positive about other aspects such as work interest, personal accomplishment, and research commitment. The university has acknowledged the results and is planning action plans to address the concerns and build on the identified strengths.

The X-47B, a tailless, jet-powered unmanned aircraft being developed by Northrop Grumman for the US Navy, successfully undertook its maiden flight, showcasing a potential future for stealthier, faster, and more advanced military drones.

Airbus has reduced the production of double-decker A380 aircraft in the coming years due to decreased demand and cutting production of A380 orders to eight in 2019. Despite this, the company is pushing an upgraded version of the A380 for potential sales, but postponed orders and reliability issues with engines from US manufacturer Pratt & Whitney remain challenges for Airbus. Despite these complications, Airbus is also involved in ongoing negotiations with Qatar Airways to resolve a recent cancellation of A350 aircraft.

The article reports that 40% of coral in the Dongsha Atoll in the South China Sea has died due to a spike in water temperatures caused by a high-pressure system, and experts warn that predictions of the future of coral reefs may be overly optimistic for shallow water reefs like Dongsha, emphasizing the need for drastic action to reduce global warming to preserve coral reefs worldwide.

Scientists have discovered a protein named Hi1a, derived from Australian funnel-web spider venom, which demonstrated potential for future stroke treatment in lab rats by blocking acid-sensing ion channels and minimizing brain damage. However, it has not yet been tested on humans, and its effectiveness as a human treatment is not known. Stroke is a brain attack caused by a cut-off or bleeding in the brain's blood supply. The research on Hi1a was published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences.

The match between Bradford City and Oldham Athletic ended 1-1, with Oldham taking an early lead through a defender's header from a free-kick, while Bradford dominated the game but struggled to convert their possession into goals. The equalizer came for Bradford in the second half after a penalty was awarded due to a foul by Oldham, with Bradford's Billy Clarke converting the penalty in the closing stages of the game.

The article reports that the experimental drug, aducanumab, has shown to be safe and may potentially halt memory decline by reducing amyloid plaques in the brain, however, larger phase 3 studies are underway to fully evaluate its effects, and experts remain cautious as there have been numerous disappointments in Alzheimer's drug development.

In a surprising turn of events, Oldham Roughyeds, a second-tier team, defeated Hull KR, a Super League side, by 28-10 in a Challenge Cup match. The Roughyeds had a commanding lead of 24-6 at halftime, and despite Hull KR's best efforts, missed conversions proved crucial in Oldham's win. Hull KR coach James Webster described his team's performance as an "utter embarrassment".

Tony Hall, BBC director general, has unveiled plans to transform the organization for the digital age, emphasizing cooperation rather than competition. The plans include an iPlayer for children, partnerships with cultural bodies, funding for local reporters to support local news, a new "Ideas Service" for educational material, and a focus on quality drama and "bigger and bolder" series. However, he warns of funding cuts necessitating closures or reductions of certain services, and the BBC may no longer need some existing services like BBC Four in the future. The proposals for collaborating with local newspapers have been met with criticism from industry bodies as they fear consolidation of news services and loss of their roles.

The Equality and Human Rights Commission has expressed concern about a rise in hate attacks, including racial, anti-Semitic, and homophobic attacks, following the UK's vote to leave the EU. The commission calls for accurate information and respectful debate from politicians, and criticizes the government's aborted plan to demand companies set out the proportion of foreigners they employ, suggesting that politicians should be aware of the impact of their words and policies on national mood. The commission also calls for a review of sentences for hate crimes in England and Wales.

In the article, Ms. Evans, who was suspended from UKIP for six months, expressed a desire to run for the party's leadership but was prevented from doing so by a small group of party leaders. She has decided to support Lisa Duffy for the position and has commented that UKIP needs internal reform, a "clean break from the past", and a shift away from its hard-right image.

The article presents an upcoming change in England's GCSE (General Certificate of Secondary Education) system, where a new grading system using numbers instead of letters will be implemented, and most subjects will be moving towards non-coursework-based assessment. The changes will apply to English language, English literature, and maths starting in 2015, and other subjects will follow suit in 2016, with the first exams in 2018. The article highlights concerns from teaching unions and educators regarding the potential confusion caused by combining letters and numbers grading systems and the potential negative impact on less academically gifted students due to the removal of coursework and the focus on final exams.

Retired General David Petraeus, who served as CIA director under Presidents Bush and Obama, indicated his willingness to serve under President-elect Trump, considering it a duty to put aside reservations based on campaign rhetoric and work for the country's best interests. He also hinted at potential closer ties with Russia as comparable to President Nixon's overtures to China in the 1970s, but with a note of caution.

The article discusses a standoff between supporters of Egyptian President Mohammed Mursi and generals who have been ruling since the ousting of Hosni Mubarak, with Hillary Clinton encouraging compromise and real politics to stabilize Egypt's fledgling democracy and ensure its alliance with the US, while also encouraging Mursi to uphold women's rights, minority rights, and the peace treaty with Israel.

Derek Bruder testified about his 1989 meeting with West Midlands Police Inspector Matthew Sawers concerning the final movements of 15-year-old Kevin Williams during the FA Cup semi-final disaster, in which he felt a pulse and attempted to revive the teenager. Bruder claims Sawers urged him to change his statement, while Sawers denies this assertion.

The anonymous band Oh Wonder, who gained popularity through releasing a song a month, found inspiration for their upcoming second album, Ultralife, after a random encounter with injured strangers on a train, which sparked a conversation about the human connections that lift people out of challenging moments.

Bertrand Traore scored a stunning goal to give Chelsea the lead against Stoke City, but the Potters fought back with a header from Diouf after Courtois failed to handle a cross, and Bojan had a chance in injury time to seal a win for Stoke. Stoke remain seventh in the table, with Chelsea 10th, three points behind them. Traore had a mixed game, while Chelsea shortened their team for the Champions League game against Paris St-Germain.

The article discusses the groundbreaking research by William C Campbell, Satoshi Omura, and Youyou Tu that led to the development of drugs for three prevalent diseases affecting more than 3.4 billion people globally, including malaria, onchocerciasis (river blindness), and lymphatic filariasis (elephantiasis). While ivermectin, derived from a soil bacterium, targets the roundworm parasites causing the latter two diseases, artemisinin, found from a traditional Chinese plant extract, combats malaria parasites. The distribution of these drugs, particularly ivermectin by Merck & Co, has significantly decreased the prevalence of these diseases. However, the emergence of drug-resistant strains in malaria continues to be a concern.

The Nelson Mandela Foundation has criticized South African President Zuma for failing leadership, looting of state resources, and damaging South Africa's democracy, as the foundation calls for accountability and for the government to be placed back in "safe and capable hands." This comes as a court hears cases involving corruption allegations against Zuma and the Gupta family, who have denied any wrongdoing. The foundation's statement comes along with growing discontent towards Zuma, with deputy finance minister Mcebisi Jonas and former ANC MP Vytjie Mentor among those who have made allegations of corruption against Zuma and the Guptas.

Miranda, a comedian and actress, performed her trademark gallop during the curtain call at the opening night of Annie at London's Piccadilly Theatre, where her performance as the drunk and vile orphanage owner, Miss Hannigan, was received with mostly positive reviews. The role takes her outside her comfort-zone, and she brings a mix of menace and humor to it. The family-friendly musical Annie, set in 1930s New York during the Great Depression, includes the songs "It's A Hard Knock Life," "Tomorrow," and "Easy Street."

In a 2-0 home win against West Ham, Shelvey, a newly signed midfielder from Swansea, demonstrated his passing, creativity, and energy, contributing to both goals. While Newcastle squandered numerous opportunities, they held on for their first victory in six league games, moving out of the relegation zone at Swansea's expense. The visitors were overpowered in the first half, with Adrian providing crucial saves to keep the scoreline respectable.

Supermarkets Morrisons, Tesco, Asda, and Sainsbury's have reduced diesel prices by up to 2p per litre, a move reminiscent of 2001 when diesel last cost less than petrol, due to lower wholesale diesel costs and increased diesel supply from refineries outside the UK. The RAC predicts further potential price cuts of up to 4p per litre for diesel over the next fortnight.

The 70th UN General Assembly, often seen as a site for African leaders to be seen and heard, is a significant platform amidst ongoing global crises, with African nations grappling with unending wars, coups, poverty, hunger, and the influx of desperate migrants. The UN, despite its flaws and controversies, has been instrumental in Africa's tumultuous past 70 years, with peacekeeping missions still present in several African countries. Current challenges like hunger, food insecurity, and the repercussions of climate change continue to plague the continent. The adoption of the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) aims to address these issues, though their implementation may be hampered by those who gather at the UN every year. Overall, the UN serves as a vital lifeline for the powerless, the hungry, and the needy across Africa.

A Public Health warning is issued as a batch of Superman-logo ecstasy pills containing the highly toxic PMMA may still be in circulation, posing a risk to consumers. It's urged not to assume different logos mean safety, and warning signs include agitation, nausea, overheating, and vision problems. Home-testing kits are deemed ineffective, so it's recommended to stay hydrated, keep the temperature down, and watch out for friends, particularly by not taking people's word for their well-being and by testing a small amount of the drug before a whole group takes a full dose.

In a letter to UKIP's leader Paul Nuttall, Leave.EU campaign chairman Mr Banks criticized the party's approach in the Stoke Central by-election, called for a return of ex-leader Nigel Farage as a key asset, and suggested changes to make UKIP more efficient, including the appointment of a CEO from industry and a new team of agents. Banks also urged for the removal of a "Tory cabal" from the party, while Nuttall's political adviser, Patrick O'Flynn, advised against donors seeking to dictate to the party leader.

An article summarized: The service Invisible Girlfriend, a platform that allows users to create a virtual girlfriend and receive text messages from a team of operators, has thousands of subscribers, suggesting a demand for such services among individuals seeking various reasons ranging from avoiding unwanted attention to practicing flirting, even though such services may be perceived as pathetic or sad by some.

Germany delivered an impressive offensive display against Poland in a 2-0 victory, showcasing the talent and versatility of key players like Thomas Muller, Karim Bellarabi, Bastian Schweinsteiger, and Mario Gotze. However, they also revealed moments of fragility in their defense, offering potential opportunities for Scotland in their upcoming match against Germany.

Blackburn Rovers and Bristol City played to a 1-1 draw at Ewood Park, with Sam Gallagher achieving a late equalizer for Rovers who remain in the relegation zone. On-loan Chelsea striker Tammy Abraham scored the opener for City before the hosts clawed their way back with multiple chances wasted by Brownhill, Taylor, and Abraham. Despite dominating the first 70 minutes, Bristol City could not maintain their lead and remain four points above the relegation zone, with future games against Barnsley, Brighton, and Birmingham. Blackburn, on the other hand, face Wolves, Aston Villa, and Brentford in their final three matches of the season. Manager Tony Mowbray was frustrated about the first goal conceded and a penalty decision that was not given, while Bristol City's Lee Johnson praised his team's performance but also criticized the lack of clinical finishing.

The Scotland national rugby team aims to send outgoing coach Gregor Townsend on a high Note, in a challenging match against Ireland, with Joe Schmidt's side having a strong record against Scotland and key players like CJ Stander proving tough opponents. The Scottish front-row, consisting of inexperienced players, faces a tough battle against Irish captain Rory Best's experienced side, but Best acknowledges the quality of the individual Scottish players.

In the Scottish Premiership match between Celtic and Kilmarnock, John Guidetti scored a free-kick after Pascali's red card for pulling back Stefan Scepovic, following which Scepovic scored a second goal after the break. Kilmarnock keeper Conor Brennan made several saves to limit the damage, but couldn't prevent the visitors from losing 2-0. The match's nature changed after Pascali's dismissal, with Celtic gaining the upper hand.

According to an international study by the Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development (OECD), Northern Irish pupils have a higher average satisfaction level with their lives compared to their peers in the UK, with 70% reporting high levels of exam anxiety, a relatively low rate of bullying, and a high rate of internet usage that is linked to lower life satisfaction. The study shows that students in Northern Ireland generally have good relationships with their parents and teachers, with about 95% reporting regular communication and support, resulting in better academic performance and higher life satisfaction. However, around one in six Northern Irish pupils experience bullying, and heavy internet use is associated with lower life satisfaction. The study also indicates gender and socio-economic disparities in life satisfaction, with girls and disadvantaged students being less likely to report high levels of satisfaction.

In a turnaround of events, Crystal Palace came back from behind after Everton's early dominance, with Romelu Lukaku scoring, to ultimately secure a 3-2 victory. Palace's resilience and self-belief prevailed even after a slow start, and they overcame an initially buoyant Everton side despite the Toffees being boosted by the fresh legs of Christian Atsu, Samuel Eto'o, and Leon Osman, making their first starts of the season. Neil Warnock's Palace showed grit and determination under his tactical leadership, leaving Roberto Martinez expressing disappointment in Everton's individual errors that ultimately cost them the game.

Gary Carter, a freelance sports journalist who traveled to London to cover the England v New Zealand rugby league match, was found with head injuries in Bethnal Green early Friday. He was admitted to the Royal London Hospital, where he underwent surgery to remove a blood clot from his brain. His wife has been receiving support from the sports community, including messages from Alan Shearer and Sam Tomkins, as Carter recovers from the attack. Police have charged James Flanagan with causing grievous bodily harm, and a 22-year-old man was arrested for affray towards attending paramedics.

Tinie Tempah, a seven-time Number One singles-scoring British artist this decade, at his studio where he's been working on his third album, Youth, for over two years, shares that his creative process was influenced by reconnecting with friends from before his success, and he notes the acceptance and success of British rappers like Stormzy and Dave in contemporary culture.

The government, Culture Secretary Maria Miller, and communications regulator Ofcom are discussing accelerating the allocation of spectrum to bring faster mobile download speeds earlier than previously planned, with the launch of 4G networks potentially happening in many places by May or June, a move which has been welcomed by mobile operator O2 but met with frustration over delays. However, the immediate advantage in the 4G race has been given to EE, with other networks waiting for the outcome of an auction, and Apple's latest iPhone is available on all major networks, but can only offer 4G speeds on the handset with EE.

The Conservative Party has decided to end the free school lunch program for young children, a policy previously introduced by the coalition government in 2014, due to concerns about cost effectiveness. This decision has been met with criticism from teachers and unions who argue that providing free breakfast instead does not address the needs of children, especially those from disadvantaged backgrounds, who may go without food for long periods during the day. The policy had a positive impact on improving food culture in some schools and addressing pupil hunger, but its abolition may erode these improvements.

A shooting took place in a busy area of Tel Aviv, wounding several people, and the suspect, an Israeli Arab, remains at large, with motives including terrorism, organized crime, or a possible hate crime unconfirmed.

Musician Dean Owens, who learned that his great great grandfather Ambrose Salvona was buried somewhere in Inverness, had his ancestor's grave found by local resident Judi Menabney after he shared the information at Perth's Southern Fried Festival. The grave was discovered in Tomnahurich Cemetery, and Salvona, who ran a circus in Scotland and was accompanied by a dancing bear, has since been found to have been a popular figure in the Highland town. The inscription on the grave acknowledges his career as a lion tamer. This discovery has influenced Owens' songwriting, with the track "Dora" on his Nashville-recorded album Into the Sea being about his grandmother, who grew up in the circus.

Glastonbury festival is introducing sustainable, recycled stainless steel pint cups for the first time on a large scale, though they lack Glastonbury branding. These cups are made from 80% recycled steel and are not compulsory; they are only available at 10 main bars out of hundreds. Despite being strong, they are awkward to throw due to their shape and lack of a lid, making them less likely to cause harm when thrown. The cups are safe to drink from, as they are made from food-grade stainless steel and cause no issues for people with amalgam fillings or dentistry associations. The cups are part of a larger effort to encourage the use of reusable products and support the UK's steel industry.

A 15-year-old boy in Nepal survived the earthquake by drinking water from wet clothes and consuming clarified butter, a woman was rescued from a collapsed building after eight hours, there's a rise in water-borne illnesses among survivors due to contaminated water, and a 11-year-old girl was also rescued from earthquake rubble. Frustration over the pace of relief efforts is growing in rural Nepal, where many villages have yet to receive aid. The UN reports over eight million people have been affected and about 70,000 houses destroyed, while dozens of countries support the aid operation.

Major financial institutions, including JP Morgan, are planning to move hundreds to thousands of jobs from London to cities like Dublin, Frankfurt, and Luxembourg in anticipation of a hard Brexit. This decision follows similar announcements by other banks aiming to secure "passporting" rights to operate across EU borders.

Police in Ferguson, Missouri, dispersed a crowd of approximately 150 protesters after a curfew started, following a shooting of a white police officer by an unknown suspect in a separate incident, and allegations of police brutality after the death of Black teenager Michael Brown by a white police officer. The unrest continued despite imposed curfew, law enforcement responded with tear gas, and there were reports of gunfire and a person critically injured.

Diane Abbott, the Labour shadow home secretary, accused Prime Minister Theresa May of allowing a decrease in police officer numbers during her tenure as home secretary, while the Conservatives defended their record and accused Abbott of having dangerous views on public safety. The debate over police resources has been a key point in the final days of campaigning before the general election, following the London and Manchester terror attacks.

In the final Test, the world champions, the All Blacks, routed Wales 46-6, recording Wales' heaviest loss in nine years and their 29th consecutive defeat against the All Blacks. Although disheartened by the results, Wales' coach Warren Gatland highlights positives learned, with a focus on improving counter-attacking skills, collision dominance at the breakdown, and adapting to the All Blacks' pace in the back three. Despite the loss, the All Blacks' coach Steve Hansen suggests a possible effect of the season's end on Wales' performance, anticipating the team's resurgence in the Six Nations.

Five individuals, including David Thomas, Stephen Thomas, Nigel Hooker, Jack Slater, and Katie Taylor, lost their lives in a boat accident in Tofino, Canada, with Stephen Thomas being a talented young photographer and a former pupil of Isambard Community School. The victims were not wearing life jackets on the open, upper deck of the boat. The Canadian government is conducting an investigation into the cause of the accident. The Canadian Joint Rescue Co-ordination Centre stated that 21 people would not have been rescued were it not for the "amazing response" by locals. A 27-year-old Australian man is still missing after the accident, and the other passengers were all in an enclosed part of the boat.

The article reports that President Thein Sein announced that a ceasefire agreement marked a historical step towards peace in Myanmar, but not all rebel groups have signed it, and concerns remain about the burmese army's adherence to the agreement.

Facebook was ordered by a High Court judge to remove a page that identified and harassed a man with a history of sexual offences in the 1980s, as the contents risked infringing his human rights. The judge granted the man anonymity but stressed it does not suppress information about his crimes already in the public domain. The man claimed harassment, misuse of private information, and a breach of his privacy rights, and filed a claim for damages against Facebook Ireland Ltd. The judge ruled in favor of the man after balancing privacy and freedom of expression, requiring Facebook to take "modest steps" to protect the man from further unlawful conduct.

Apple is encouraging publishers to join a new app service, but the service terms are automatically assumed accepted unless publishers opt out. The terms require publishers to indemnify Apple in case of legal claims and allow Apple to place ads next to publishers' content without payment. Apple will use RSS feeds to distribute content, which publishers make publicly available voluntarily. The service is categorized under Apple's marketing department and is expected to launch later this year. Controversy has arisen over the opt-out approach, with some publishers expressing concerns that they may inadvertently be bound by the agreement.

Guam, a US territory with a US airbase and about 6,000 troops, along with 165,000 civilians, is named as a potential target for North Korean rockets due to its proximity. While there is increased concern among some residents, not everyone is fazed by the situation, with some referring to the ongoing threat as a "situation they've been living with for a couple of years."

The Sentinel-1b spacecraft, carried into orbit by a Soyuz rocket, is a new addition to the Copernicus program of the European Union. Sentinel-1b will work alongside Sentinel-1a, and together they will map the entire Earth every six days, providing extensive data for applications ranging from environmental monitoring to infrastructure planning. The satellites will carry laser communication systems for data transfer. Other satellites, including the fundamental physics experiment Microscope, were also launched on the same rocket. Microscope is aimed at investigating the equivalence principle, examining the rate at which different materials fall in the vacuum of space.

The article suggests that the pound has gained 1% due to market predictions that Theresa May may win a larger majority in the June snap election, which could potentially lead to a less harsh Brexit plan, causing the pound to strengthen. However, the stock market is down because UK's large companies derive much of their income from foreign currencies, and a stronger pound reduces the value of those earnings in sterling terms. The election is seen as providing Theresa May with more breathing room and increased certainty, although business groups have varying opinions on the implications.

A hiker, Pavlina Pizova, got lost while hiking the Routeburn track in Fiordland National Park and, due to bad conditions, her companion Ondrej Petr slipped and died. After staying with his body for a night, she moved on to find shelter and spent another night out in the open. She then stayed in a hut for nearly a month before being found by a search team. She was later interviewed by police, and Petr's body was recovered and a coroner's inquiry launched.

Elena, a 40-year-old Muscovite, and her family live below the poverty line due to two decades of accumulating debt from multiple banks, a common struggle for millions in Russia. Despite plans to amend bankruptcy laws, debtors like Elena often receive no help, with banks unwilling to restructure debts and few individuals having financial protection. The financial burden often impacts families, with elderly relatives also taking on debt to help their struggling relatives. Such incidents highlight the harsh realities of capitalism in Russia, as regulations and protection for debtors remain inadequate.

On July 30, Judge William Sylvester denied an expanded media coverage request for James Holmes, accused of opening fire at a Batman movie premiere, killing 12 and wounding 58.
