The court appearance of the accused was filmed, despite objections from his legal team, and he appeared dazed with dyed orange hair. The suspect is reportedly forced to wear a face guard and has been linked to explosive materials found in his apartment, including 30 grenades and several gallons of gasoline. Public appeals to avoid using the suspect's name continue, including Jessica Ghawi's brother who lost his sister in the shooting. The Batman star, Christian Bale, visited victims in hospital, while a pregnant woman who escaped the shootings gave birth to a baby boy. The shooting has led to calls for stricter gun control in the U.S., but with elections approaching, legislative efforts are unlikely in the near future.

The Art Recovery Group, which has recovered over $500 million of stolen and looted art over the past decade, is working to help stop the theft of Syria's precious antiquities by fighting against the smuggling of artifacts out of the country, increasing awareness among collectors and dealers, using databases to help identify and report looted objects, and partnering with law enforcement agencies worldwide.

Despite the prediction-worthy magnitude of the 2011 Fukushima Daiichi Nuclear Power Plant disaster, the commission found major flaws in safety standards and emergency procedures due to systemic issues like ignore societal conventions, regulatory inefficacies, negligence, and operator misconduct. The report emphasized and lamented the mindset responsible for this "manmade disaster."

The article outlines that small businesses have achieved a high compliance rate (95%) in the latest stage of the government's auto-enrolment programme, which requires providing pensions to employees aged 22 and above who earn more than £10,000 yearly. The process is gradual, with 66% of employees enrolled, and includes workers such as nannies, care workers, plumbers, and bar staff. Employers and employees contribute to the pension pot, with the average current employer contribution at 3%. Some experts argue that the rates are "woefully inadequate" for ensuring a decent retirement, and a review of the system is planned to address this concern, with minimum contribution rates increasing from 2% to 5% in April 2018 and to 8% in April 2019. Additionally, concerns have been raised about certain trusts that administer pensions for small firms.

The article discusses a new calculation of the quantity of modern groundwater (6% of the total water stored in the first 2km of Earth's surface) and highlights its significance as a vital but finite resource that is rapidly renewed, sensitive to climate change, and human contamination. This study, led by Dr. Tom Gleeson, provides a global view of modern groundwater distribution, emphasizing the need for sustainable management, especially given its uneven distribution worldwide.

The European Challenge Cup finals will take place in Edinburgh, Scotland in 2017, with the host stadium yet to be confirmed. This decision was made by European Professional Club Rugby, and it is seen as a nod to the success of Scottish Rugby, particularly after the previous European Cup finals in 2005 and 2009 at BT Murrayfield. The Champions Cup finals will be held in Lyon, France, with both events taking place over the same weekend. The announcement has been welcomed by Scottish Rugby officials, club coaches, and the Scottish Government.

Edward Snowden, wanted by the US for leaking details of surveillance programs, will remain in the Moscow's Sheremetyevo airport's transit zone as his application for temporary asylum in Russia is still being processed, according to his lawyer Anatoly Kucherena. Snowden, who has been staying at the airport since arriving from Hong Kong on June 23, is currently unable to leave without receiving the travel documents. Despite requests from the US for Snowden's extradition to face espionage charges, Russia has yet to decide on his status.

Brazil's Attorney-General Rodrigo Janot has requested an investigation into former president Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva's alleged involvement in a multi-billion dollar corruption scheme at state-oil company Petrobras, known as Operation Car Wash. The allegations against Lula involve suspected illicit benefits received in the form of renovations on a luxury apartment and a ranch for his family, as well as payments for speaking fees or donations from construction firms implicated in the scandal. The specific charges against Lula are not yet known, though obstruction of justice is suspected. The investigations are based on testimony given by Senator Delcidio do Amaral as part of a plea bargain. If charged, the pressure on current President Dilma Rousseff, who nominated Lula as her chief of staff, would increase significantly.

The article summarizes that the families of three SAS candidates, who died from hyperthermia during a selection exercise in 2013, believe that holding the Ministry of Defence legally accountable would result in improved safety measures in military training, but the UK government sees no need to amend the 2007 Corporate Manslaughter Act as it currently has effective safeguards in place to learn from fatalities and discourage failure.

Leicester City, last season's Premier League champions, are struggling in the league and faced relegation-threatened defeat by League One side Millwall in the FA Cup, despite Millwall playing with 10 men for most of the second half. Manager Claudio Ranieri emphasized the need for fighting spirit and stronger performances, with Leicester currently performing poorly and one point above the relegation zone, risking becoming only the second defending English champion to be relegated.

The article discusses HMRC investigating dozens of footballers, agents, and football clubs for potential irregularities in their tax affairs, particularly concerning image rights income paid into offshore accounts, and notes ongoing criminal investigations and the formation of an inter-agency task force, with the case of football manager Jose Mourinho being recently under scrutiny.

A controversy has sparked in Germany over the investigation of journalists for treason after publishing classified documents revealing expansion of online surveillance, highlighting a national debate about press freedom, government influence, and privacy rights, with government leaders pressured to dismiss the prosecutor.

The Chancellor's Budget speech predominantly focused on boosting growth in regions such as Greater Manchester, Aberdeen, and the Midlands, as part of a drive to build a "northern powerhouse," with very little focus on the South East region, leaving political opponents criticizing a potential increase in the north/south divide, as well as accusations of complacency towards voters in the South East.

In a tough match where Colchester United stifled Doncaster Rovers' passing game, the hosts narrowly took a 1-0 lead into half-time thanks to a late Tommy Rowe goal. Despite mounting pressure from Colchester in the second half, Doncaster held on for the win.

Royal Bank of Scotland's CEO, Ross McEwan, says in an interview with BBC Newsnight that uncertainty around the EU referendum is causing problems for UK banks, slowing down business, and he hopes the vote will take place in June. McEwan does not foresee a Bank of England interest rate rise before 2017, citing prolonged low interest rates as a new normal. He also shares that RBS has turned a corner under his leadership, although it is likely to post its eighth consecutive year of losses, and the bank remains in public ownership with the British government holding a majority stake. McEwan expresses doubt about the possibility of repaying the £45bn bailout funds from 2008 and mentions ongoing legal costs related to mortgage-backed securities and payment protection insurance.

At the 2015 general election, the Labour Party is emphasizing unity, a strong economy, and creating change, while opposing any deal with the SNP due to moral and principled reasons. The SNP is focusing on the need for more progressive policies from a potential minority Labour government. The Conservative Party is promoting a strong economy and maintaining Scotland in the UK. The Liberal Democrats are highlighting mental health services and aiming to hold politics in the center ground, focusing on keeping the economy on track and avoiding a second independence referendum.

A team of students, Elliot Vale and Tia Mountain, have designed an app called GeoRescue, which aims to provide information on natural disasters and guide people to safety using advanced maps services and GPS, potentially saving lives. The app is set to present at a space conference in Manchester and be pitched to a Dragons Den-style panel in June, with the intention of turning it into a fully-working app. The idea was inspired by a recent avalanche in the Arctic Circle, where Elliot Vale was studying, which highlighted the risks of living in a dangerous environment.

The proposal in Scotland's Higher Education Governance Bill to directly elect the chairs of universities' governing bodies, including the position of the rector, has been strongly criticized by Sir Timothy O'Shea as inconsistent, incoherent, and potentially damaging, particularly for one of Scotland's major universities. The Scottish government acknowledges these concerns and will continue to consult with all interested parties.

Elena Hrabovenska, a Ukrainian woman who runs a Polish deli in Huntingdon, England, receives a note expressing support from British customers following racist hate mail amid the Brexit referendum. Her main concern is the potential escalation of such hate speech to physical violence. She shares her journey of starting her business and the irony of a non-Pole owning a Polish deli, while also facing supply chain disruptions due to migrant gridlock at Calais. She anticipates that shops like hers will become less common as the newer generation integrates into the British community.

An anonymous threat led to increased security measures at the Dallas Police Department headquarters following the shooting death of five white police officers by a black man, Micah Johnson, during a protest rally against police killings of black men earlier in the week. Johnson was a supporter of black militant groups and stated he wanted to kill white police officers. The bloodshed followed the killings of Philando Castile in Minnesota and Alton Sterling in Louisiana, and has prompted continued protests and gun attacks against police and civilians in various parts of the US. Despite the threats and recent violence, protests such as the "Weekend of Rage" in Philadelphia, organized by the Black Lives Matter movement, are planned to continue.

Australian Prime Minister Abbott agrees to increase the number of Syrian asylum seekers but stops short of broadly increasing refugee numbers. Members of his party, including state premiers, advocate for more action for refugees, and the Opposition calls for 10,000 additional Middle Eastern refugee places. State leaders have expressed concerns, with NSW Premier Baird calling for broader action beyond ending boat arrivals. The government has faced criticism for offshore processing of boat migrants.

Nigel Farage, UKIP leader, argued that the UK could not achieve its target to cut net migration while being a member of the EU, claiming that the government had been dishonest about this matter. He advocated for a "return to normality" with a net migration of about 30,000 people per year, and accused the Conservative and Liberal Democrat parties of planning to "rig" a potential EUreferendum.

Former England Under-21 manager Gareth Southgate, with a track record at Middlesbrough and as the FA's head of elite development, is appointed as the permanent England manager, commencing with a friendly against Germany on 22 March. His tactical understanding, leadership and player relations are highlighted as strengths, and he is determined to create a team appreciated by English fans.

The FBI is demanding Apple disable the security software on a murdered terrorist's iPhone, but the tech giant has refused. Supporting Apple's stance are Mark Zuckerberg, Google, Twitter, and others in the tech industry, who argue against creating backdoors to encryption. Former Judge Stephen Larson, representing victims of the terrorist attack, is urging Apple to cooperate, but Apple's CEO, Tim Cook, has described the FBI's order as "dangerous" and "unprecedented." The FBI Director, James Comey, insists the demand is in support of the victims and justice, wanting to use the phone to potentially find more terrorists without breaking encryption or creating a master key.

The article describes the various ways that Queen Elizabeth II celebrated her 90th birthday, including Meeting staff at the Royal Mail delivery office, official events, and a new bandstand opening, as well as and political leaders wishing her a happy birthday. It also details a BBC interview with Prince William, where he pays tribute to the Queen as a "guiding example" and discusses his own commitment to royal duty, and mentions the release of new stamp featuring the Queen, as well as the Republic's criticism of the BBC for focusing on the royal family and not being fair, balanced, and proportionate in their coverage.

Zachary Quinto, Chris Pine, and John Cho have expressed support for the inclusion of an LGBT character in the Star Trek universe, while George Takei has disagreed, arguing that Hikaru Sulu's sexuality "twists" the original vision of the creator Gene Roddenberry who always envisioned Sulu as heterosexual. The film Star Trek Beyond includes a brief scene of Sulu being greeted at the end of a voyage by his male partner and daughter.

Peterborough United defeated Bristol Rovers 4-1, with Jack Marriott scoring a treble and Rory Gaffney scoring a consolation goal for Rovers, while Tom Lockyer hit the bar for Rovers and Junior Morias, Steven Taylor, and Chris Forrester contributed goals for Peterborough.

The article reports that jihadists attempted to seize control of strategically important Tadmur on the edge of the ancient city of Palmyra, a UNESCO World Heritage site, but were halted by the Syrian army. The director of Syria's antiquities warned that if IS took control of Palmyra, it would repeat the destruction it had wreaked on other ancient sites in Iraq.

On a high-speed Thalys train from Amsterdam to Paris, members of staff were accused by passenger Jamie Robinson of abandoning passengers by locking themselves away in a service room during a terrorist attack, while the heroic actions of some American passengers were widely praised.

The British Olympic Association (BOA) has upheld the selection of Muhammad, ranked 59th in the world, over world number one Aaron Cook by GB Taekwondo, despite criticism of the process and potential for legal action from Cook's camp. The BOA has emphasized the need for improved communication with national governing bodies regarding selection policies for future Games.

Hannah Witheridge and David Miller, both aged 23 and 24 respectively, were found dead on a beach in Koh Tao, Thailand. The investigation into their murder has reached a dead-end, as forensic tests showed DNA from two unidentified men on Witheridge's body, none of which match the DNA of Miller, the Ware brothers, or 11 Burmese suspects previously questioned. The police have admitted they are at a loss as to how to proceed with the investigation, and are now looking for a group of men who were heard singing Western pop songs near the crime scene. The investigation's lack of progress has been compared to past cases of murdered British people in Thailand.

Japan plans to increase the popularity of rugby union by hosting the 2019 World Cup and Olympic Games in Tokyo, focusing on efforts to increase awareness and participation, particularly among young people, using digital media, school programs, and professional teams to spread the rugby experience and engage a wider audience.

The article suggests that the outcome of uprisings in Arab countries is determined not solely by the demand for democracy but also by the role and behavior of the military, or army. Independent, professional armies with a distinct corporate identity can contribute to peaceful transitions, while armies that are extensions of autocratic regimes may respond with violence. Ethnic differences within an army can also play a significant role in its actions during uprisings.

Unemployment rate fell to its lowest since 2005, with 1.68 million people out of work, while average weekly earnings grew by 2%, a slow increase that fell below expected growth. The employment rate reached a record high of 74%, and economic inactivity fell to a low not seen since 2014. Despite these improvements, economists suggest that an interest rate hike is still unlikely due to low inflationary pressure.

Middlesbrough earned a 2-0 home win against Bournemouth, with goals from Gastón Ramírez and Stewart Downing, despite earning only seven goals in their first nine matches. Bournemouth had chances, with Josh King hitting the crossbar, but failed to match the intensity of their performance against Tottenham in their previous game.

In the first practice session of the Chinese Grand Prix, Williams driver Felipe Massa suffered two left-rear wheel failures, and Renault's Kevin Magnussen had a suspected broken left rear suspension. Williams identified a problem with the "rim clearance," and both teams kept their cars in the pits for the remainder of the session. Meanwhile, Lewis Hamilton and Nico Rosberg topped the times, with Hamilton facing a five-place grid drop due to a gearbox change. Fernando Alonso returned to McLaren after missing the last race, and ended the session 12th fastest.

Hibernian routed Bonnyrigg Rose 8-1 in the Scottish League Cup thanks to a dominant first-half performance that featured three goals in 13 minutes from Shinnie, Keatings and Humphrey, along with two from Cummings in the second half.

The article reports that Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni has criticized the parliamentary speaker for passing a bill that criminalizes homosexual acts without a quorum and emphasizes his position that homosexuality is unacceptable but not a reason for persecution. This new law would expand the Penal Code's ban on male homosexual acts to include female-to-female sex and make it illegal to identify as a homosexual or provide services to them. The bill aims to create a legal framework for banning homosexuality and has faced criticism from human rights activists both inside and outside Uganda.

Manager Slade aims to guide Cardiff City to a top-six finish in the current season, a feat which would surpass any achievement in his career thus far, though he fondly recalls his play-off campaigns with Grimsby, Yeovil, and Leyton Orient, particularly a 5-4 victory over Nottingham Forest in the semi-finals with Yeovil. Despite expressing confidence in reaching the final, he humorously mentions that he has yet to win a play-off final, and may need to rely on his club's CEO for the final if they make it that far.

Scottish Women's Footballer of the Year, Evans, playing for Bayern Munich, expresses anxiety about missing a third consecutive play-off for major competitions, as Scotland, currently ranked 22nd, aim to secure their place in the Euro 2022 finals by winning this Friday's game against 20th-ranked Iceland, the group's top seeds. Their second encounter is scheduled for September 20th. Having more players in top leagues, like Evans in the German Bundesliga, is seen as beneficial for the national team.

Claire, a former event-rider, determined to regain her independence after a spinal injury, is using a robotic walking suit to complete the London Marathon, which will take her about three weeks to finish. Despite the challenges, she hopes to improve her speed and raise over £50,000 for Spinal Research. Her competitions include a race against her one-year-old daughter to walk unaided, and she is receiving encouragement from Matt Hampson, Tim Henman, and Lucinda Green.

Jack Walsh, a 23-year-old filmmaker from Northern Ireland, is working for the popular Game Grumps channel in Los Angeles, where he shoots and directs commercials and contributes to their planned expansion into TV comedy on YouTube's Red channel. His passion for film was ignited by his A-level course in moving image arts, and he moved to Los Angeles at 18 to study at film school. He has worked with renowned composer John Debney and written and directed his own short film musical. Despite the growth of Northern Ireland's film industry, particularly with Game of Thrones, Walsh is not yet ready to return home.

The Scottish First Minister is ranked 50th on Forbes' 2016 list of the world's most powerful and influential women, with the German Chancellor Angela Merkel topping the list for the 6th year in a row. Merkel's leadership and decisive role in the European Union placed her ahead of U.S. Presidential hopeful Hillary Clinton and Janet Yellen, the Chairwoman of the US Federal Reserve. Other notable women on the list included the Queen, the co-founder of the Bill and Melinda Gates Foundation Melinda Gates, and Mary Barra, President of General Motors.

The article discusses a research, published in the journal Conservation Biology, that finds many mammal species are sensitive to ultra-violet (UV) light, and their avoidance of power line corridors could be due to the UV-rich flashes or corona that occur when charge builds up in cables. This global issue could potentially disrupt wildlife migration and habitat patterns. The research suggests power companies may need to consider measures to address this problem.

A former employee told the BBC that staff at Kids Company, a charity providing support to vulnerable youth, were informed of complaints about a client who sexually exploited girls he met there, but didn't pass on the concerns or alert authorities.

The article discusses a Brexit voter, Paul Austin, who initially advocated for Brexit, but, a year later, has become more ambivalent due to concerns over immigration policies, taxation, EU court access for individual cases, quality checks for imported goods post-Brexit, and observing a shift in perspective towards the UK from other Europeans.

England nearly pulled off a remarkable win in the first Test against Pakistan, with debutant Adil Rashid playing a key role in taking five wickets. Chasing 99 to win, England struggled to find boundaries despite a strong top-four performance from Jos Buttler, Ben Stokes, Joe Root, and skipper Alastair Cook. The match ended in a draw, 25 runs short of a victory, due to fading light and Pakistan's effective use of spin bowling and fielders on the boundary. England's earlier mistakes, such as dropped catches and a no-ball leading to a dismissal, proved costly. Despite the draw, England put on a vastly improved overseas performance compared to their previous tours, with Cook's record-breaking 263 in the first innings and a strong batting partnership between Cook and Moeen.England's new-look opening partnership and promising performances from Rashid and Moeen Ali give them confidence going into the second Test in Dubai, which begins on Thursday.

Celtic manager Brendan Rodgers was pleased with the performance of recently signed French midfielder Olivier Ntcham, deeming him capable of playing at the highest level, and also praised another new recruit, Kundai Benyu, for his impressive displayed during a recent friendly match against Lyon. Rodgers credits Ntcham for his versatile range of passing and competency in both short and long passes, dribbling, and shooting. Benyu, on the other hand, has apparently impressed Rodgers with his technical skill, mobility, and competitive edge, earning a spot in the Celtic squad.

A plane carrying 300 initial doses of GSK's Ebola vaccine, intended for a trial involving 30,000 volunteers, is en route to Monrovia. The vaccine has shown initial favorable results, but whether it provides adequate protection against the virus can only be determined in affected countries. Other trials for other vaccines and drugs are planned, but decreasing Ebola case numbers pose a challenge for testing.

In the match between Blackpool and Wycombe Wanderers, both teams had multiple opportunities to score but failed to find the net, resulting in a 0-0 draw. There were several attempts missed, efforts saved, and shots hitting the woodwork and going wide. Briefly yellow cards were shown to Paul Hayes (Wycombe Wanderers) and Danny Pugh (Blackpool).

The Australian government reached a last-minute settlement of A$70 million with 1,905 claimants allegedly harmed while held on PNG's Manus Island between 2012 and 2016, with the settlement aimed at avoiding a potentially expensive and uncertain court trial, despite ongoing criticism of the offshore refugee detention policy.

Paul Scholes, a legendary midfielder who spent his entire career at Manchester United and won numerous titles, has returned from retirement to help the team cope with midfield injuries, much to the delight of manager Sir Alex Ferguson. This unexpected comeback came less than an hour before United's match against Manchester City, where Scholes played for the final 31 minutes, contributing to a 3-2 victory.

A Welsh creator, best known for the creation of the beloved children's cartoon character SuperTed, has produced a feature-length animation, Norm of the North, and is currently working on a film about former Cardiff City football club legend Robin Friday, emphasizing his passion for Cardiff City even from his Hollywood base.

The rise of right-wing, nationalist parties across Europe, such as Austria's Freedom Party (FPOe), Denmark's Danish People's Party (DPP), Finland's Finns Party, France's National Front (FN), Germany's Alternative for Germany (AfD), Greece's Golden Dawn, Hungary's Jobbik, Italy's Northern League (Lega Nord), and the Netherlands' Party for Freedom (PVV), among others, is reshaping Europe's political landscape by capitalizing on discontent about immigration, globalization, and the perceived weakness of the establishment. These parties often advocate for stricter immigration policies, anti-EU sentiment, and traditional national values.

Spurs chairman Daniel Levy defended a lack of summer signings, arguing against "unsustainable" spending, while Conte stated that unless Spurs aim for titles or the Champions League, they shouldn't expect to be considered a tragedy. Despite not adding any new players, recent history suggests that Spurs may traditionally finalize most of their deals in August. Chelsea have spent about £130m on three players, with Conte expressing interest in Tottenham's Harry Kane, valuing him at around £100m.

The article discusses increasing numbers of drunken passenger arrests, cases of physical abuse against cabin crew, and the ineffectiveness of a voluntary code of conduct on disruptive behavior, leading calls for stricter alcohol regulations at UK airports, with some suggesting making it illegal to consume one's own alcohol on a plane. The Home Office is considering potential changes, while airport authorities argue that the sale of alcohol itself is not the problem but its misuse.

The British Racing Drivers' Club (BRDC) has announced that Silverstone, home of the British Grand Prix since 1987, may not be able to host the race after 2019 due to financial losses, but both parties are working towards a deal to ensure the event's continued presence at the venue.

Marcus Rashford scored a late winner for Manchester United versus Hull City, securing all three points and maintaining United's and Chelsea's 100% records in the Premier League. United out-performed Hull, who had rare chances in the game, primarily through former MU assistant manager Mike Phelan's resilient team.

Ben Stokes, who was suspended from the 2014 World Twenty20 for punching a dressing room locker and infamously clashed with Marlon Samuels, has expressed his desire to maintain his aggressive cricket style while acknowledging the need to temper it at times. He has recently been named vice-captain of the Test team under Joe Root. England, who have won 9 of their last 10 ODIs against West Indies, face the Caribbean side in their upcoming series, with Stokes expected to start in his first series since becoming the most expensive foreign player in the Indian Premier League. West Indies, ranked ninth in the world, will field an inexperienced team due to changes in national selection. England captain Eoin Morgan is focusing on the Champions Trophy in June, but acknowledges that West Indies could pose a tough challenge due to their powerful batting lineup and challenging pitch conditions.

At Coventry City College, staff with backgrounds in vocational trades have been teaching GCSE English and maths to underachieving students to help them advance in their careers. Despite minimal success with these subjects in school, some students are now succeeding with this new approach, crediting the more one-on-one and personalized attention they receive, as well as the importance of the GCSEs in their future careers.

Vaughan Gethin, the Welsh Transport Minister, has expressed disappointment over Network Rail's investment levels, alleging insufficient funding has led to inadequate autumn leaf clearance, causing damage to train wheels, overcrowding, and reduced punctuality. The issue was discussed during a Senedd debate, with Plaid Cymru's Adam Price labeling the conditions as a "national crisis." Network Rail, however, maintains they are working to maximize value for taxpayers' money by collaborating with Arriva Trains Wales.

The Committee discussion covered various topics including Brexit, devolution, steel industry, funding, and the Severn crossings. On Brexit, Alun Cairns acknowledged challenges but saw potential advantages in focusing efforts on new international trade opportunities. No changes to the Wales Bill are planned other than those previously signaled, and there are no plans to change the Barnett Formula. The dropping of the commitment to hold a referendum before Wales gets income tax powers was addressed, with Cairns emphasizing its importance as part of devolution policy. On the steel industry, Cairns expressed optimism about a potential joint venture between ThyssenKrupp and Tata Steel Europe. The government has no plans to make a profit from the Severn crossings once they return to public ownership.

In the T20 Blast, Durham Jets pulled off an unlikely victory against Leicestershire, with Paul Collingwood (34) and Paul Coughlin (38 not out) chasing down a Luke Ronchi-inspired 88-2 for Leicestershire, despite Collingwood and Jack Burnham being run out in the final over. Elsewhere, Hampshire beat Gloucestershire by 24 runs thanks to James Vince (42) and Rilee Rossouw (45), and Michael Klinger scored a magnificent unbeaten 101 for Gloucestershire, while many games were rained off, including Sussex vs Middlesex and Lancashire vs Nottinghamshire.

China, led by Mao Zedong, transitioned from a stagnant communist regime to a fast-growing economy following Mao's death and subsequent economic reforms, with today's China being one of the world's largest economies, a top exporter, and investing heavily overseas. Despite the economic boom, social and environmental issues, along with human rights concerns and tensions surrounding territorial disputes, persist.

Betting has been suspended for Ellie Goulding to perform the Spectre title track due to her cryptic Instagram post indicating she has been working at Abbey Road studios. Other favourites include Radiohead, but no official announcement has been made by the makers of Spectre regarding the artist for the theme song.

The Scottish government, under the leadership of Nicola Sturgeon, is planning for a referendum on Scottish independence in the future, but not in 2017, as a response to the UK's decision to leave the EU. Sturgeon aims to negotiate a "soft Brexit" or a special arrangement for Scotland to remain in the EU single market, but if these efforts fail and there is a hard Brexit, she may consider a referendum sooner rather than later. However, critics like Scottish Conservative leader Ruth Davidson have called the delay in referendum planning an "empty gesture."

Four individuals, Bakr Hamad, Shahif Kadir, Zana Rahim, and Awat Hamasalih, have refused extradition in a UK court, as they are accused of being part of an international jihadist network allegedly seeking to establish a caliphate in Iraq's Kurdistan region. The network is reportedly connected to the radical Islamist group Ansar al-Islam and is said to have provided logistical and financial support for the recruitment of foreign fighters to be sent to Syria and Iraq. The group is also accused of intending to train these fighters for a future conflict in Kurdistan.

The IFS's Green Budget indicates that the UK is planning the largest fiscal consolidation among 32 advanced economies, with departmental spending cuts of £51.4bn (14.1%) needed in the next parliament, but the report suggests that the UK economy is expected to have zero inflation and 3% growth this year, and the prognosis is optimistic due to a big turnaround in household finances over the next year. The report also illustrates the central economic choices at the upcoming elections: bigger cuts from a Tory or Tory-led government vs higher public sector debt with a Labour government, with both parties aiming to protect spending on health, education, and overseas aid.

In the football match between Cambridge United and Cheltenham Town, Luke Berry scored a hat-trick, while Uche Ikpeazu and Billy Waters (for Cheltenham) also found the net, with the final score being 3-1 in favor of Cambridge United.

A controversial bonfire in a public car park in Belfast, which poses a risk to health and safety for nearby residents, has led to court injunctions, complaints about offensive materials, and political debates about cultural traditions and hate crimes. Sinn Féin leaders have criticized the burning of political flags and symbols, while the Democratic Unionist Party defends the tradition as part of unionist culture. Meanwhile, authorities are investigating complaints about distasteful materials on various bonfires, including a racist message directed at a Celtic footballer.

The article discusses how broadcasters are using technology to engage viewers, notably through companion apps for shows during key moments, utilizing audio watermarking and smartphone/tablet interfaces. These apps increase viewer interaction, offering features like trivia, behind-the-scenes content, and even predicting show outcomes, and thus may increase ad revenue. Broadcasters are also exploring future possibilities in interactive television, such as a TV screen that integrates with a smartphone for content selection and viewing.

The article discusses the political pressure on tech companies like Facebook and Google to remove hateful content from their platforms, particularly in light of a recent attack in Finsbury Park mosque. However, it raises concerns over the difficulties in managing vast amounts of content and the potential challenges in granting these companies increased censorship powers, as well as the moral implications of private companies taking on a role traditionally reserved for the government.

The article describes Longford Town Centre, once envisioned as a commercial cathedral during Ireland's economic boom, now standing as a symbol of the country's economic downturn. Local trader Matt O'Brien sees a turnaround in his business, thanks to diversifying into childrenswear and a substantial dress-hire business. However, criticism is levied at the government for not effectively addressing the region's needs, particularly in terms of investment, while local politicians are hopeful about a proposed Center Parcs development as a potential boon for tourism and the economy.

The experimental aircraft, Solar Impulse, with a wingspan larger than a jumbo jet and weighing only as much as a large car, piloted by Mr. Borschberg, is attempting a five to six-day non-stop solar-powered flight across the Pacific to reach Kalaeloa airport on Hawaii's O'ahu island, potentially setting aviation records. The mission, part of the plane's quest to circumnavigate the globe using only solar energy, has faced delays due to unfavorable weather conditions over the ocean. The journey entails continuous flight with limited sleep and constant meteorological and flight strategy updates. Despite preparation for potential emergencies, such as ditching in the Pacific, the pilot will not risk electrocution by remaining aboard in such a scenario. The Solar Impulse project aims to demonstrate the potential of clean technologies rather than promoting a specific future for aviation.

Lord Carey, a former Archbishop of Canterbury, has dropped his opposition to the Assisted Dying Bill due to the reality of needless suffering, particularly following the case of Tony Nicklinson. Despite Archbishop Justin Welby's warning that the bill could lead to pressure on vulnerable individuals, Lord Carey feels it's not "un-Christian" to allow people to take their own lives when they're suffering at the end of their lives. This change in stance from Lord Carey could have significant consequences for the debate in the House of Lords and within the Anglican church.

The article discusses various suggestions and reactions on social media regarding how to prevent North Korea's recent claimed H-bomb test from escalating into an international crisis. Ideas range from increasing global cooperation on weapons, inviting North Korea to talks, enforcing sanctions, preparing for potential threats, and considering a more subtle approach to address the issue while acknowledging the moral complexities of other countries' nuclear weapon stockpiles, with some suggesting former NBA player Dennis Rodman, who has had personal connections with Kim Jong-un, could potentially play a role in negotiations.

Refugees and asylum seekers living in Belfast, including a former Algerian police officer named Mohammed, spend their free time as volunteers in the Mourne mountains, County Down, rebuilding dry-stone walls and repairing mountain paths as part of a program with the Mourne Heritage Trust. The conservation work helps the refugees find tranquility, improve their English, and make new friends, while also benefiting the Trust by offering much-needed labor.

Stuart Broad's exceptional 5-wicket haul within a single spell, under challenging conditions, along with England's team efforts, turned the third day of the match from a promising situation for South Africa into a resounding defeat for them, highlighting England's growing prowess as a top cricket team.

The article discusses a comprehensive continent-wide analysis of the groundwater resource in Africa, revealing vast reserves primarily in northern African sedimentary basins. While the researchers warn against large-scale drilling for sustainable water supplies, they stress the potential for low-yield boreholes and careful extraction for drinking water and community irrigation purposes, especially in semi-arid regions. Essential for mitigating water scarcity and climate change impacts, these groundwater reserves could significantly aid some of the world's most vulnerable populations.

Lord O'Donnell, a former UK cabinet secretary, forecasts that it will take "years and years" for Parliament to fully separate from Brussels, with his "central assumption" being that the EU will not undergo radical changes. He suggests that a looser, broader association with the EU might be a possibility for the UK. O'Donnell also states that Theresa May, the current Prime Minister, faces a challenging task in determining the type of Brexit that best serves the British people and in implementing it.

A 22-year-old woman, Sian O'Callaghan, is missing following a night out, and a search led by local volunteers and police is underway in Savernake Forest near Marlborough, with a £20,000 reward being offered and CCTV footage of her last known movements being released to the public.

Ferrari showed promising pace during the second practice session for the Chinese Grand Prix, with Kimi Raikkonen leading Mercedes driver Lewis Hamilton by a significant margin, hinting that they may pose a threat to the Mercedes team. However, doubts remain as Ferrari has previously failed to match their practice form in qualifying this season. Other notable mentions include Hamilton's difficult day, Fernando Alonso returning after missing the last race, and a number of technical issues for several teams.

Arlene Foster is joining a campaign calling on Germany to acknowledge its moral and financial responsibility towards Thalidomide survivors, who were born with birth defects due to the drug and are seeking compensation for their struggles. A representative of the campaign, Kim Fenton, a former mayor in Northern Ireland, shares her personal battle with the drug's long-term effects, including dislocated hips, deteriorating health, and financial strain.

Actor Eli Wallach, born in 1915, had a six-decade-long career starting in 1956, earning him a reputation for versatility and being a "quintessential chameleon." He gained fame as bandit chief Calvera in The Magnificent Seven, Tuco in The Good, the Bad and the Ugly, and Mr. Freeze in the 1960s Batman series. Despite never being Oscar-nominated, he received an honorary Academy Award in 2011 for his body of work. Wallach continued acting into his 90s, passing away in 2012.

Hanson Academy, under a stricter uniform policy enforcement, sent home nearly 10% of its pupils on Tuesday for not meeting the standards, causing frustration amongst parents, with many questioning the school's communication and financial implications. The principal believes these rules are an integral part of preparing students for adult life and improving conduct, behavior, and respect within the school.

Violence erupted in Beirut between Sunni pro- and anti-Syrian groups following the shooting death of two anti-Syrian clerics, marking the first such incident in Beirut since Syria's conflict began last year. Despite deep divisions over Syria, Lebanon has thus far managed to avoid more widespread violence, but Sunday's incident could escalate tensions.

The article discusses Nick Clegg, the former leader of the Liberal Democrats, arguing during the 2015 general election campaign that only a new stable and strong coalition involving his party could ensure stability and prevent another election, as the hardening positions of Labour and the Conservatives on coalition deals could lead to a more unstable minority government. He also stated that the Liberal Democrats would not make any deals with UKIP or the SNP.

Liverpool suffered a stunning second-half collapse in the UEFA Europa League final against Sevilla, failing to maintain their lead and conceding three times in a 24-minute span, which results in them not qualifying for any European competition next season. Manager Jurgen Klopp accepted responsibility for the performance and assured fans they will come back stronger. Criticism was directed at both left-back Alberto Moreno for his repeated errors, and former manager Brendan Rodgers for not adequately strengthening the left back position during his tenure.

In the West Midlands, a man named Ikram Elahi was killed, and three others were injured, with a 25-year-old in critical condition, following a violent incident in Sparkbrook involving a gun and knives. Police are investigating, urging witnesses to come forward and assuring the community that there are no further threats anticipated. The area has been marked as a crime scene, and locals expressed worry about their safety and well-being.

South African President Jacob Zuma's government is investigating 17 banks, including Barclays, JP Morgan, and HSBC, for colluding and manipulating currency markets through coordinated fictitious bids since 2007. The Competition Commission has recommended fines equating to 10% of each bank's local turnover. This alleged manipulation, if proven, could further tarnish the sector's reputation and may lead to prosecution at the Competition Tribunal. The investigation is significant as it highlights an ongoing ethical crisis in South Africa's banking sector.

On Tuesday, Arlene Foster's economic advisor, Mr Robinson, denied any family links to the Renewable Heat Incentive (RHI) while admitting his father-in-law applied to the scheme, and denied any personal interest or role in the business. Similar denials were also made by special advisers named by MLA Jonathan Bell, who alleged that they blocked him from reducing the tariffs on the RHI scheme due to their extensive interests in the poultry industry, and that they tried to prevent Arlene Foster from being called to the Public Accounts Committee. MLA Bell made these allegations under parliamentary privilege, and he has kept records to support these claims. Some advisers of the DUP, including Mr Robinson and Dr Crawford, have family members with connections to the poultry industry, but not to the RHI scheme. MLA Bell was later suspended from the DUP after making these allegations.

The new technique using CRISPR gene editing allows for the creation of a molecular tape recorder that uniquely and indelibly marks cells with a "barcode" in DNA, which can be used to trace all a cell's descendants, providing profound insights into biological development, including the origins of diseases and inherited disorders, and potentially aiding in understanding cancer formation and metastasis.

The man was denied permission to block the department's plan to publish another list of RHI (Renewable Heat Incentive) recipients, despite his claim of potential reputational damage and business losses, as the department deems the risk as "tenuous" and within their rights. The RHI scheme, intended to encourage heat creation from renewable sources, has been oversubscribed, leading to a scandal and a projected overspend of £490m that caused Stormont's institutions to collapse. The applicant, a business owner who invested £100,000 in a boiler, was accredited to the capped scheme, and his annual payment barely exceeded the limit to avoid naming. He argued the publication of recipients' details would not distinguish between those on the capped scheme and those with earlier, more generous tariffs. The department plans to include the date of application in the published information, allowing the public to discern the applicable tariff and showing the applicant did not join during a high-volume application period in Autumn 2015. The department is set to publish this information next week.

Judge Thokozile Masipa sentenced Oscar Pistorius to five years in jail for culpable homicide for shooting and killing his girlfriend Reeva Steenkamp, following trial proceedings that lasted longer than expected. The athlete and amputee sprint double amputee Olympic and Paralympic Games participant is expected to serve about 10 months with the remainder under house arrest, depending on good behavior. The sentencing received mixed responses, with some viewing it as too light and others as fair. The Steenkamp family expressed relief that the case was over, while the Women's League of South Africa's African National Congress suggested they might pursue an appeal, considering it a message that committing crimes such as femicide might result in a slap on the wrist.

The article describes how the beach where Tunisia's worst terrorist attack occurred has reopened, but the emotional scars from the tragedy still persist, particularly for those who were directly affected, such as 57-year-old Sabi who runs a boat club on the beach. The tourism industry in Tunisia is struggling due to thousands of holidaymakers leaving on emergency flights after the attack, and many people are nervous about returning to the beach despite efforts by some to stay and support the country. The attack is just one part of a broader challenge facing Tunisia, including a rise in Islamist attacks, disorder from neighboring Libya, and concerns over the number of Tunisians fighting in Syria and Iraq. The attack has dealt a significant blow to the tourism industry, which contributes 15.2% to Tunisia's GDP and supports over 473,000 jobs. The article invites readers to share their stories related to the Tunisia attacks.

British Foreign Secretary Philip Hammond's visit to Tripoli mainly aims to support the nascent Government of National Accord in Libya, providing them with £10 million in aid and further practical assistance for countering terrorism, combating people smuggling, and promoting stability in Libya. The discussions regarding a potential 6,000-strong European military force under Italian command remain uncertain, with concerns about potential targeting of these troops by local militias and terrorist groups. Key European military players, like Britain, may be compelled to assist Libya, considering its growing threat to southern Europe and broader implications for European security.

The Beyond Caravaggio exhibition at the National Galleries in Scotland showcases artwork from over 30 European artists influenced by the revolutionary Italian artist Michelangelo Merisi da Caravaggio, including his masterpieces The Taking of Christ (1602) and The Supper at Emmaus (1601). The exhibition, which also features works by artists such as Ribera and Gentileschi, traces the impact of Caravaggio on the early 17th-century art world. One notable work in the exhibition, The Taking of Christ, was rediscovered in Dublin in 1990 and was recently loaned to the Scottish National Gallery. The exhibition runs from June 17 to September 24 and costs £12 for admission.

Two men, Virgilio Correia (aged 35) and Christopher Menaul (aged 27), were sentenced to at least 16 and 9 years in prison respectively for the murder of Wing Fu Cheung (64) in January 2015, as well as additional time for wounding with intent and robbery. Portuguese national Correia and Menaul were found to have committed the murder while under the influence of drugs, needed the money for a drugs debt, and attacked the Cheungs as they drove home after closing their Chinese takeaway restaurant. Correia's actions were described as "catastrophic" and led to an "orgy of violence." Their accomplices, Gary and Lisa Thompson, were also jailed for assisting the killers and perverting the course of justice, while Mrs. Cheung, who was also wounded and robbed, returned to Hong Kong with the couple's children. The judge expressed sympathy for the lasting impact of the incident on the Cheung family.

County cricket is undergoing changes, including less Championship matches, a structured T20 Blast during school holidays, and a Lord's one-day knockout final in July, to appeal to younger audiences and maintain the sport's popularity as the current generation ages. These changes aim to streamline the schedule, reduce format changes for players, and improve the T20 Blast's visibility for broader appeal. Former England captain Michael Vaughan encourages the T20 Blast to be more accessible on terrestrial television.

US economy grew at an annualized rate of 2.6% for the fourth quarter, exceeding the annual growth for 2014 as a whole, with a significant contribution from increased consumer spending driven by lower fuel prices, while business investment saw a decline.

The article explains that the failure of the Welfare Reform Bill in Stormont has led to a delay in devolving the Corporation Tax to Northern Ireland, causing companies to postpone decisions to invest due to the uncertainty over the tax rate. This uncertainty may result in low investment, net emigration, and increased unemployment if the Corporation Tax is not reduced to match the Irish rate of 12.5%.

Chris Rea, a multi-million album-selling singer-songwriter, gained a unique F1 experience when he worked as a mechanic for Eddie Irvine during the 1995 Monaco Grand Prix. This led him to collect racing memorabilia and release an album featuring historic footage chronicling his passion for the sport, particularly for the iconic driver Wolfgang von Trips. Despite his fame in music, Rea considers himself a genuine F1 fan.

Margaret Thatcher, famously known as the Iron Lady, was a divisive yet transformative prime minister of the United Kingdom, who governed for 11 years from 1979 to 1990. She introduced significant changes to government policy, such as privatizing state-owned industries like British Gas and BT, promoting home ownership through council house sales, and strengthening London as a global center for banking and business. Her historical achievements include leading the defense of the Falkland Islands, though this also led to significant loss of life. However, she faced substantial opposition, particularly from strikes and protests over policies like the closure of coal mines, job losses, and the poll tax. Thatcher is remembered as a key figure in modern British history, who had a significant impact on shaping the country for over two decades.

The mental health tribunal has deemed that Ian Stewart Brady, the notorious serial killer who, along with Myra Hindley, was convicted for the murders of five children, continues to suffer from a mental disorder and requires continued treatment at Ashworth Hospital. The decision denies Brady's request to be transferred to a Scottish prison, as the tribunal determined it would be clinically necessary for him to remain at the facility for his own safety and treatment. Brady, who has been on a hunger strike since 1999 and recently testified at the tribunal, has the right to appeal if he can show that the tribunal misapplied the law.

Domenico Scala, a member of Fifa's Ad-Hoc Electoral Committee, is being challenged by the Liberian Football Association (LFA) boss, Musa Bility, to withdraw due to potential conflict of interest arising from shared nationality with one of the presidential candidates, Gianni Infantino. Bility has threatened to take the matter to the Court of Arbitration for Sport if Scala does not step down by Thursday. However, Scala's spokesperson asserts that there is no conflict of interest this time as there is no incumbent president among the five candidates.

Brock Turner, a former swimming champion, was released from jail after serving a third of his sentence for sexually assaulting a woman outside a Stanford University fraternity house. This release occurred amid public outcry, criticizing the lenient sentence, with many calling for the recall of the judge involved. The victim's case was notable, with a witness seeing the assault and the attacker not admitting the crime. A new California law aims to close the loophole that allows for lenient sentences without use of force in sexual assault cases.

The trial of Stephen Beadman and Luke Harlow is ongoing at Nottingham Crown Court, where both men are charged with false imprisonment in the death of Kayleigh Haywood. Harlow had earlier pleaded guilty to sexual grooming, two counts of sexual activity with a child, and attempting to meet two other underage girls for sexual purposes. The prosecution alleges that on the night of November 13th, 2015, Kayleigh went willingly to Harlow's flat in Ibstock, Leicestershire, and had told her family she was staying with her best friend. However, the trial heard that Kayleigh was given substantial amounts of alcohol, was sexually touched, and was held against her will by both men. The murder weapon, Beadman, took her out of the flat and later admitted to police where her body was found in thick undergrowth near a stream.

The BBC article discusses the UK's European Union referendum results, highlighting a significant divide between the north and south of England, with many northern voters choosing to leave the EU as a rejection of the perceived metropolitan elite. In Scotland, the results may trigger a second referendum on Scottish independence, while in Birmingham, the results were close and divided communities. In the South West, farmers expressed satisfaction with the vote, while in Hartlepool, a voter summarized the general mood as a vote against the establishment. The consequences and implications of the vote remain unclear for many regions.

Train workers are set to strike for 24 hours starting Monday evening over pay and job disputes, leading to limited or cancelled services on Scotrail, Gatwick and Heathrow Express lines, Southeastern, Virgin West Coast Mainline, and other companies like CrossCountry Trains, Chiltern Railways, Arriva Trains Wales and First Great Western. The strike could affect football fans traveling for the Championship play-off final at Wembley. Negotiations continue with Network Rail and union leaders.

The Rugby Football Union (RFU) proposes shortening the Six Nations tournament from seven weeks to six, with concerns raised over player safety and potential damage to athlete health, as this condensed period would reduce training time. Additionally, there's an independent review of Wales' controversial 100-minute defeat by France in the Six Nations, as concerns around firmly enforcing rules for player safety and integrity remain.

Scottish Labour Party leader Johann Lamont resigned, accusing the UK party leadership of treating Scotland as a "branch office" and not recognizing the Scottish party's need for autonomy. Former Scottish Labour leaders, including Jack McConnell and Henry McLeish, expressed anger and disappointment at the treatment of the Scottish Labour Party and the undermining of Lamont's position. McConnell called thedevelopment "astonishing" and accused the UK party leadership of not having a positive vision for the 21st century, while McLeish said Labour in Westminster lacked understanding of Scottish politics.

Multiple European champions were crowned this weekend, including Club Brugge in Belgium, Benfica in Portugal, and Besiktas in Turkey. Elsewhere, Benfica secured a domestic title with a record points total, while Stuttgart was relegated from the German Bundesliga. In France, Steven Fletcher scored and missed a penalty in his potential final Ligue 1 game for Marseille. Sevilla lost their final La Liga game without an away league win, and Sporting Gijon avoided relegation in Spain. The "will he stay or will he go" saga of Roma legend Francesco Totti's future remains unresolved.
The National Audit Office report criticizes the Department for Education for being unprepared for the rapid expansion of academies, leading to an £1bn overspend on the programme.

The government requirement that key nursery workers have at least a grade C in GCSE English and maths is causing a drop in the number of students completing Level 3 Early Years Educator courses, potentially leading to a staff shortage, recruitment crisis, and affecting the quality of childcare on offer. Industry leaders fear this could jeopardize government plans for 30 hours of free childcare for all three and four-year-olds.

A review of Donald Trump's political campaign statements shows a range of controversial positions, including support for waterboarding, a desire for Mexico to pay for a border wall, calls to restrict Muslim immigration, and embracing a view that terrorists would be contained more effectively by former leaders such as Saddam Hussein.

The article emphasizes that effective planning, deep understanding of one's business, hard work, passion, digital mindset, diversification, active listening to customers, innovative strategies, a good team, constant innovation, risk-taking, unique marketing, and disciplined focus are all integral to succeeding in business.
